t.Weirwater: Weirwater's senator proposed the tomb, and once it is complete, congregations in Weirwater will receive a Philtre of Strength every season.

r.Weirwater/Sandling: Sandling was chosen as the site of Ozren Orzel's inspirational tomb, a three-month great work built of white granite.

Construct Spy Network in Tsirku.d: Rahmah i Darwisj i Erigo, as Imperial Spymaster, announced the commission of a spy network in Tsirku under the words "To unseen shores". The project needed 10 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns in labour, and took three months to finish. After the Winter Solstice Aengel Dunn supplied 3 thrones, 4 crowns and all 10 wains of weirwood, while Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven gave a crown each. The network is now complete, and military units can support it to investigate Tsirku.

t.Tsirku: Tsirku, held by no one at the time, now has an Imperial spy network that military units can support to investigate the territory.

Construct Trencher's Shining Ambition.d: Proposed by the senator for Kallavesa and seconded by Reikos, the motion commissioned a great work benefitting fleets. It required 20 wains each of white granite and weirwood, 10 wains of mithril and 180 crowns in labour, raised by its marshland site, plus standard costs, with three months to complete. Trencher Smoulder in The Cold supplied all the materials and 21 thrones 2 crowns after the Winter Solstice. Triska Markova, Farren Silver Streams and Rhys Nighthaven added small sums. With the lighthouse complete, all fleets in Kallavesa gain an additional rank when trading.

n.Wintermark: A Wintermark territory gained a great lighthouse that strengthens the trade of its fleets, funded largely by Trencher Smoulder in The Cold, in a bid to revive Westerhal's commerce.

t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa's own senator proposed the lighthouse, and now that it is complete every fleet in the territory gains an additional rank when engaging in trade.

r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: West Marsh is the site of Trencher's Shining Ambition, a great lighthouse whose marshland location raised its labour costs.

Construct Wayhouse in Holberg.d: Using an Imperial Wayleave, Ciapek Splintered Oak announced a wayhouse in the marshes of Utterlund. It required 16 wains of white granite and 1152 rings in labour, a cost raised by building in a marsh, and took three months to complete. Ciapek provided the granite and 6 thrones after the Winter Solstice. Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg, Farren Silver Streams and Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn added smaller sums. Once completed, the wayhouse allowed Navarr to take a personal resource in Holberg without the foreign nation penalty. It also created the title of Keeper of the Splintered House, first appointable at the Spring Equinox 388YE by unanimous decision of Navarr's senators.

n.Navarr: The Navarr gained a wayhouse in Holberg, letting their people take personal resources there without the foreign nation penalty. Their senators can appoint its Keeper by unanimous decision from Spring 388YE.
n.The League: A Navarr wayhouse was raised in the League territory of Holberg, and Kaspar Yakovich von Holberg contributed money towards its construction.

t.Holberg: Holberg gained The Splintered House, a Navarr wayhouse that opened the territory to Navarr personal resources without the foreign nation penalty.

r.Holberg/Utterlund: The Splintered House was built in Utterlund's marshes, which made the labour more costly. It now stands there as a completed wayhouse.

Construct Well of Life.d: The commission required 40 wains each of white granite and weirwood, 20 wains of mithril and 60 crowns in labour, with six months to complete. Donations were recorded after the Winter Solstice 387YE and the Spring Equinox and Summer Solstice 388YE, mostly materials from Fausta Ankarien plus money from many individuals. Once complete, the Well of Life would add 15 mana crystals to the Conclave font each season and provide a large hospital. It would cheapen the Grandmaster's mana purchases and let them buy vital honey. It would also improve local herb gardens, give order members true vervain and the vaults ilium, cut Imperial army casualties in Madruga, Kahraman, Segura and Feroz by a tenth, and create the Freeborn title Hakima of the Rippling Marshes.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Feroz, then held by Grendel, is one of the territories where Imperial armies would suffer a tenth fewer casualties once the Well of Life is complete.
n.The Brass Coast: The great lodge would stand in Freeborn Madruga, giving Imperial armies fighting across Brass Coast territories reduced casualties and creating a new Freeborn position, the Hakima of the Rippling Marshes.

t.Feroz: Imperial armies fighting in Feroz, then in Grendel hands, would suffer a tenth fewer casualties once the Well of Life is complete.
t.Kahraman: Imperial armies fighting in Kahraman would have their casualties reduced by a tenth once the hospital is complete.
t.Madruga: Madruga would host the Silver Chalice's grand lodge, gaining a large hospital, improved herb gardens and reduced casualties for Imperial armies fighting in the territory.
t.Segura: Imperial armies fighting in Segura would suffer a tenth fewer casualties once the Well of Life is complete.

r.Madruga/Lightsea: Lightsea is the site chosen for the Well of Life, the Silver Chalice's grand lodge and hospital, which would be overseen by the new Hakima of the Rippling Marshes.

Construct the Story Garden.d: Announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, Master of Rings, the Story Garden cost 12 wains of weirwood and 36 crowns in labour and took three months to complete. Lady Nineve Orzel provided 4 thrones 3 crowns and the weirwood, and Daugon Deliquio Orzel added 1 crown. The tenured title of Apothecary of the Story Garden receives bladeroot and was first available for appointment at the Spring Equinox 388YE by unanimous decision of Dawn's senators. The Constitutional Court ruled this appointment method unconstitutional, holding the title should be appointed by the Apothecaries Guild; under its guidance the title can still operate and be re-elected normally, but cannot be amended without addressing the appointment issue.

n.Dawn: Dawn gains a new tenured title whose holder brews potions for virtuous Dawnish citizens in return for tales of their deeds, funded by Lady Nineve Orzel and appointed by unanimous decision of Dawn's senators, though the Constitutional Court ruled that method unconstitutional.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the construction was announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, the Master of Rings.

t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar appears only in the name of Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, the Master of Rings who announced the motion.
t.Weirwater: The Story Garden sinecure was built at Belletain in Weirwater, using 12 wains of weirwood and 36 crowns of labour.

r.Weirwater/Sandling: Sandling became home to the Story Garden at Belletain, completed after three months, where its Apothecary trades potions for stories of virtuous acts.

Crimson and green.d: After the Autumn Equinox the vallorn's assault on the west faltered, possibly because of an ettercap poison used in Sweetglades. A Spring ward woven over Eastring by the Voice of the Quiet Forest drew the vallorn there instead. It overwhelmed the Druj defenders, absorbed the ward and claimed the region. The Thimble weirwood grove is now cut off. Agents of the Prince with a Thousand Foes freed some Druj slaves, including nearly a hundred former Imperial citizens. The vallorn, now at 19,000 strength, is waning but will try to expand for one more season. When Thornsong House's ward failed, the Druj burned it. The apothecaries fled carrying lore, and an opportunity arose to rescue them.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Sun withdrew to Astolat after fighting the vallorn in Peakedge Song, and its earlier losses inflicted on the Druj help buy the fleeing apothecaries time.
n.Druj: The Druj lost Eastring and its garrisons to the vallorn, with fugitives slaughtered in Sarangrave. Their remaining forces in Therunin, mostly in East Ashes, are cut off and desperate, though a Druj band burned Thornsong House and is hunting its apothecaries.
n.Highguard: The Wolves of War withdrew to Bastion after Peakedge Song. Highguard's Reikos and the Gardens of High Chalcis are the refuge the Thornsong apothecaries are fleeing towards.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Apothecaries' Guildhouse would have slightly lower upkeep if built in Skarsind.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven appears only in the further reading list of earlier vallorn winds.
n.Navarr: The Navarr see the vallorn take Eastring and the Thimble weirwood grove, which can now only be recovered by linking the vallornhearts. Nearly a hundred captured Navarr and other former citizens were freed, while their apothecary college at Thornsong House was burned and its people hunted.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn's earlier advance had threatened the northern regions of Morrow, but that threat eased when it turned east.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Sun withdrew to Astolat after the Autumn Equinox.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War withdrew to Bastion after the Autumn Equinox.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Brocéliande is cited as the fate awaiting Therunin, lost to the vallorn, if Tharunind is left to expand freely.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven appears only in further reading about earlier victories over its vallorn.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is not named directly and is touched on only through the wider Navarr struggle against the vallorn.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn's surge had posed a threat to northern Morrow, which receded when it turned on Eastring.
t.Reikos: The surviving Thornsong apothecaries are fleeing towards the Reikos border and High Chalcis, where a band of Druj lies in wait. If rescued, they would support a new college of potions there.
t.Sarangrave: Druj fleeing the vallorn in Eastring ran into the Nesustak Forest rebels and their allies, and few survived. Freed slaves, both humans and orcs, also reached Sarangrave.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Apothecaries' Guildhouse would cost less upkeep if built in Skarsind.
t.Therunin: The vallorn claimed Eastring and the Thimble, and Thornsong House burned. The weakening vallorn may still take more of the territory before the Spring Equinox, and the cut-off Druj cling to four regions.

r.Sarangrave/Bendol: Mentioned in passing: Bendol appears only in further reading about an earlier expedition, Into Béantal Dol.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: Druj escaping Eastring fled into the Nesustak Forest, where the rebels and their preternatural allies killed most of them.
r.Therunin/East Ashes: East Ashes holds most of the remaining Druj forces, trapped behind Imperial lines, and is seen as the likeliest target for the vallorn's final season of expansion.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Eastring was overrun by the vallorn, which destroyed the Druj garrisons and absorbed their Spring ward. The region gained the vallorn quality and can only be reclaimed by linking the vallornhearts, and the Thimble is now isolated within it.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: After costing nearly two thousand Imperial lives here, the vallorn's assault on Peakedge Song receded once the armies withdrew.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: An Imperial expedition through the Sentinel Gate to Sweetglades found a poison that burns through ettercap nests. It may explain why the vallorn turned away from the west.

Death leaves us homesick.d: A military treaty put the Gates of Ipotavo in the field in Sarangrave, and the Axou plan to take the Tower of the Skink and evict the orcs of Thornfen, expecting the Empire to deal with them. The Grand Council refused to join any plan to wake the vallorn of Visokuma. Kaban arrested the Scions of Cavan, self-proclaimed Navarr cousins accused of plotting to unleash it, and their leader begged for Imperial help. Navarr fleets met a cold reception in Axou ports. Theodosia of Ipotavo's Unified Convocation condemned the Synod over Fintan's execution. In the end the Scions were executed, the Navarr did not back a rescue raid, and the Assembly of the Way invited Axou priests to collect Fintan's remains.

n.Druj: The Axou were fighting the Druj in Sarangrave under the new treaty, with a Druj fortress standing between them and the Imperial armies. They planned to take the Tower of the Skink once the Druj were defeated.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Navarr jailbreak was compared to the Imperial Orcs' earlier freeing of the Tamazi from the citadels.
n.Navarr: Suspicion over the vallorn left Navarr fleets with a cold reception and reduced production in Axou ports. Some thorns urged a rescue raid into Kabanja to save the Scions of Cavan, but the Navarr did not back it and the Scions were executed.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: a League assembly statement on Axou soldiers visiting the Five Cities Military Academy and the Barossa School had gone largely unnoticed in Axos and lacked legal backing.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Axos is described as lying south-east of Urizen, and the Assembly of the Nine is quoted warning that rousing the vallorn would raze Axos.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Ambassador to Axos, Thanmir Hrafnar, is of Wintermark.

t.Sarangrave: The Axou Gates of Ipotavo were fighting the Druj here under the treaty, and Axos intended to claim the Tower of the Skink and evict the orcs of Thornfen. A proposed Navarr raid into Kabanja would have been launched from here.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Axou interest in sending soldiers to the Barossa School of Imperial Strategy is noted as an unanswered matter.

r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: The Axou declared that once they held the Tower of the Skink they would first evict every orc living in Thornfen, including those at Sephals. They assumed the Empire would deal with relocating them.

Each age a lens.d: A meeting hall was completed on Gull Isle, west of Kallavesa. Igya Olgafsdottir proposed a hetjuveisla at the Spring Equinox, with Iron Osric, the Golden Jarl and the Imperial Consul, to agree terms of war. The Synod might consecrate part of the hall, with Wintermark endorsement. Speaker Morna said the Grendel do not seek peace and demanded withdrawal from Mareave and Redoubt as a minimum. Morajasse offered mercenary service against the Iron Confederacy and faced spying proposals. Beoraidh confirmed Sarcophan protection, offered investments, and sent a delegation while aggrieved gladiators sought retribution. The Druj demanded Imperial withdrawal from Sarangrave.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Rahvin orcs in the Barrens are cited as keeping to themselves, with an uncertain relationship to their Imperial neighbours.
n.Druj: A buruk tepel named Inkagoch demanded that the Empire withdraw from the Sarangrave, threatening that the Tainted Basilisk would destroy the warding stones of Béantal Dol and unleash the vallorn.
n.Grendel: Speaker Morna told the new ambassador that the Grendel do not desire peace. Any serious Imperial offer must at minimum include complete withdrawal from Mareave and Redoubt.
n.Imperial Orcs: Diamant Drakes gladiators from Beoraidh vowed retribution at the Winter Solstice against the Sannite Sand Vipers they accuse of assaulting them. A separate Beoraidh delegation sought to meet the Imperial Orcs and Senator Pathfinder Gaddak.
n.Jotun: The Jotun helped raise the new Meeting Place and filled it with an ancestral shrine. Igya Olgafsdottir proposed a feast of heroes at the Spring Equinox to negotiate how the war with the Empire will be fought.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: there were undercurrents of unhappiness in Navarr that Winterfolk and Freeborn would negotiate the terms of war with the Jotun.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn of Feroz and Segura continued to refuse trade with the orcs of Morajasse, whom they associate with Rahab's tyranny. The Jotun's unnamed 'Golden Jarl' is a Freeborn figure invited to the war negotiations.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: messages reached the Consulate in Tassato, and the former Grendel of the League are cited as orcs within an Imperial nation.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's long-standing peace treaty with the Thule is noted, with their diplomacy covered in a separate wind of fortune.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Starlight Starchaser, the new Ambassador to the Grendel, received Speaker Morna's letter. It made clear that no peace is possible without Imperial withdrawal from Redoubt and Mareave.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: a renegade Varushkan destroyed and defiled the old Meeting Place in 382YE, and orc septs remain in Ossium.
n.Wintermark: With Wintermark Assembly support, the new Meeting Place was completed. Winterfolk Iron Osric and Consul Atte Arrow-Tongue were invited to the Jotun feast, with Ingrid Talon-of-the-Mark responsible for it. The Jotun also asked the National Assembly to guarantee any consecration of the site.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Grendel espionage rings are known to operate throughout the Bay, and Beoraidh and the Delves remain free to pursue their ambitions there.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun still dominate Bregasland, fuelling Marcher discontent that they were not named in the war negotiations.
t.Feroz: The Grendel protectorate in Morajasse continued to guard the territory and offered to fight the Iron Confederacy for pay. Options were raised for spies, scouting armies or the Silent Bell to investigate it.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: Hordalant is not named on the page; it is relevant only as part of the Jotun nation involved in the proposed negotiations.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman is not named on the page; it is relevant only as part of the Brass Coast, whose Freeborn feature in the Jotun and Morajasse diplomacy.
t.Kallavesa: The new Meeting Place stands on Gull Isle, a wave-swept tidal island in the waters west of Kallavesa. It is the proposed site of the Spring Equinox feast with the Jotun.
t.Liathaven: A Jotun messenger from Ashvale, as the Jotun call Liathaven, camped under a flag of truce at the burial mound of Fort Braydon to deliver Igya Olgafsdottir's proposal.
t.Mareave: Lord Ehsan of Beoraidh confirmed Sarcophan protection and offered a temple, dock investment and a consulate. The Grendel demanded Imperial withdrawal from Mareave as a minimum condition for peace.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: some orc septs remain in Ossium, having declined the offer to move to Skarsind.
t.Redoubt: The Grendel hold parts of Redoubt and insisted that complete Imperial withdrawal from it be part of any serious peace offer.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: The Druj ultimatum came from Inkagoch, a buruk tepel residing in the city of Leen in the Salt Flats.
t.Sarangrave: The Druj threatened to have the warding stones of Béantal Dol destroyed, unleashing the vallorn across the marshes, unless all Imperial forces withdrew. The civil service warned the loss of life could be apocalyptic.
t.Segura: Quartermasters from Mora's Rock tried to buy supplies from the Freeborn of Segura but met suspicion and little success.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the old Jotun–Wintermark Meeting Place, just outside its borders, was destroyed in 382YE.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial attack on Skallahn threatens to take the Kongegőr bridge linking the Jotun's northern and southern territories.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the remaining orc septs of Ossium declined the offer to move to Skarsind.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Consulate in Tassato received the messages from Morajasse, Beoraidh and the Druj.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Rahvin orcs living in the Barrens are noted as having an uncertain relationship with the Empire.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Druj work with the vallorn in Therunin is cited as evidence of their advancing understanding of it.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Spring Equinox meeting honours Tromsan traditions of hospitality.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The islands remain occupied by Iron Confederacy forces. Commander Gallum offered to fight them if well paid, and a spy network could gather information on the Suranni there.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: Commander Gallum Fiersach and Wind Lord Saoirse hold Mora's Rock, asking to deal with the Imperial Consul. Saoirse renewed her offer to enchant the fortress, while the Empire weighed ways to spy on the protectorate.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Mentioned in passing: the Senate recognised the Morajasse protectorate after the battle at Oran.
r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Lord Ehsan announced a treaty of protection with the Sarcophan Delves. He offered the Empire a temple, dock investment or a consulate, while sending a delegation and facing gladiators bent on retribution.
r.Mareave/Sinfoyard: Under Beoraidh's treaty, any attack on the plains of Sinfoyard will be treated as an attack on the Sarcophan Delves. The proposed Imperial consulate would stand there.
r.Tromsa/Tromsdalen: The proposed meeting follows the Tromsdalen custom of the hetjuveisla, a feast of heroes at which feuding warbands set aside blood-price to negotiate how the coming battle will go.

Every day of your life.d: Bloodcrow Knott's judgement, upheld with a greater majority (60-46), asked for an Assembly of the Ancestors with civil service support. The Court found no constitutional basis for it. Any such assembly would also be almost entirely Imperial Orcs, and only a Senate constitutional motion ratified by the Throne could change this, with dim prospects. Three opportunities followed. The Illarawm offered to carve the words of one ancestor each season onto the Grand Ossuary's walls. The Yerende Black Tillers offered to trade the Legion's Rookery's liao for Hearkeners Hope, an ancestor-communion narcotic; this offer has since expired. For a year, the Assembly could also mandate shamans to study a non-Imperial sept's ancestors.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: named among the barbarian orcs whose ancestors the Empire knows little about, with travel into Druj lands noted as especially dangerous for any delegation.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: named among the barbarian orc septs whose ancestors are little known, and Apulian orcs in the League are said to have embraced the Virtues rather than their Grendel ancestors.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs' call for an Assembly of the Ancestors was judged constitutionally impossible, but it revitalised interest in their ancestors. Their Assembly gained options to record ancestors' words in the Ossuary, to accept Hearkeners Hope in place of liao (now expired), and to send delegations to study other septs' ancestors.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: listed among the barbarian orcs about whose ancestors the Empire has learned few secrets, making their septs possible subjects for an Imperial Orc delegation.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr using the wayhouse in Skogei Glens could theoretically have shared in the Black Tillers' Hearkeners Hope.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: listed among the barbarian orcs whose ancestors remain largely unknown to the Empire, and so a possible subject for an Imperial Orc delegation.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Wintermark Assembly's Chronicle of Heroism is cited as a precedent for the proposed Annals of the Ancestors.

t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: Hearkeners Hope is said to be prepared from rare plants not unlike those used by the mystics of Kallavesa.
t.Skarsind: The Illarawm offered to carve honoured ancestors' words onto the Grand Ossuary in Skarsind. The Legion's Rookery could have been altered to give Skarsind's congregations Hearkeners Hope instead of liao, though that offer has since expired.

r.Skarsind/Skogei Glens: Mentioned in passing: Navarr visiting the wayhouse in Skogei Glens could theoretically have received Hearkeners Hope under the Black Tillers' proposal.

Every path you know.d: In 388YE the Navarr Assembly may, by Synod mandate, choose a different nation each season to share their skills with, creating an opportunity for a new title aiding the Vallornguard. Three commissions are proposed. Restoring the First Voice Glade botanical garden in Oakways would return 27 herbs a season to the Dean and let them upgrade a Vallornguard member's herb garden. A Vallornguard Mustering Ground in Holtford would create the First Thorn title and let an army resupplying in Miaren take the Uproot the Aberration order. Kaela offers to patronise the Grim Pyramid in Old Ranging, with a 3,000-strong garrison, but only if Hercynia swears never to rebuild Hacynian and the Senate cedes it to her.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction notes the Grendel still pushing Navarr soldiers back during a wet season under Rivers of Life.
n.Navarr: Navarr's Assembly can send people to a different nation each season to share their hard-won knowledge of fighting the vallorn, and its people may commission a herb garden, a mustering ground and, if Hercynia swears to abandon Hacynian, Kaela's Grim Pyramid.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the civil service warns that if the Grim Pyramid were ceded to Kaela, her grim legion could cause trouble for the Wintermark territory of Hahnmark.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the civil service cautions that a Kaela-controlled Grim Pyramid with its grim legion could cause significant trouble for Hahnmark.
t.Hercynia: Kaela will back the Grim Pyramid in Hercynia only if its folk swear, through a proposed Synod mandate, never to rebuild the Terunael city of Hacynian, an oath whose breaking would carry severe consequences.
t.Miaren: Chosen for being firmly Imperial yet central to the Empire's vallorn hearts, Miaren could host both a restored herb garden at the First Voice Glade and a Vallornguard Mustering Ground that strengthens armies resupplying there.

r.Hercynia/Deer's Folly: Kaela's price is an oath that the ruins of Hacynian in Deer's Folly will be left to time, with no new city ever raised there or named Hacynian.
r.Hercynia/Old Ranging: The Grim Pyramid, an inverted stone pyramid thirty floors deep in the Starless Vale, could be built here with a 3,000-strong garrison of grim legionaries defending the region unless sent to fight alongside an Imperial army.
r.Miaren/Holtford: A Vallornguard Mustering Ground could be built in Holtford to drill recruits against vallornspawn, creating the First Thorn of the Vallornguard and enabling an army resupplying in Miaren to take Uproot the Aberration.
r.Miaren/Oakways: The botanical gardens of the newly rebuilt First Voice Glade School in Oakways could be restored, giving the Dean 27 herbs a season and the power to upgrade a Vallornguard member's basic herb garden.

Everything is trying to kill us.d: Imperial and Druj armies were still fighting over the Sarangrave. A Vigilant fervour, inspired by Urizen's victory over the recidivist sword scholars, let the Urizen Assembly pick one problem and one archetype each summit. The investigators would not solve the problem themselves but would bring forward opportunities the following season; appraisals could speed this up. The problems were a hostile populace with rebels holding Nesustak Forest, a venomous lowland marsh where ushabti cannot work, miasma pillars in all but one region, and little Urizeni appetite to settle. Irra Harah was also stirring the rebels, a huge vallornheart was walled up by Druj wards, and Kroll's Spring guardian had been defeated but not slain.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish Assembly's judgement inviting the rebel septs to break bread with them appears to have gone unnoticed, and the bloody legacy of the Barrens feeds the Sarangrave's hostility towards the Empire.
n.Druj: The Druj were still campaigning to retake the Sarangrave. Their hidden miasma pillars, lifelong propaganda, walled-up vallornheart and the fed monster of Kroll were all burdens left for the Empire.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel-held Mareave is referred to in the opening dialogue as an arid land.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: their sept-by-sept approach to settling Mareave is held up as the model Urizen should follow.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the text notes that even a Bregas might balk at moving to the Sarangrave.
n.Navarr: Urizen had committed to working with the Navarr towards destroying the vallorn. The Navarr were named as the best source of aid against the Sarangrave's vallornheart, especially if their national assembly offered support.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Urizen's loss of Spiral is described as the reason the Sarangrave felt like a consolation prize.
n.Urizen: Urizen took on the Sarangrave and faced years of costly work to make it prosper. Its Assembly could set one archetype each season to investigate the territory's many problems.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Bregas are invoked as people who might still balk at the Sarangrave's marshes.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: Mareave serves as the precedent for incorporating a newly won orc-populated territory, and is described as arid.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is not named; it is covered only by the general point that Urizen's mountain spires are a world away from the Sarangrave.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Mentioned in passing: Urizen curses unleashed here without regard for the inhabitants are cited as fuel for Druj propaganda.
t.Sarangrave: The newly Urizen territory was still contested and faced many problems: hostile inhabitants, deadly marshland, miasma pillars, few willing settlers, Irra Harah's meddling, a caged vallornheart and the monster of Kroll.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Urizen displaced from Spiral are cited as weary of moving again, and its loss frames the Sarangrave as a consolation prize.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the bloodshed of the Barrens is cited as a warning, and its tragedies shape how Sarangrave's people see the Empire.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Urizen forced from Zenith are among those tired of resettling.

r.Sarangrave/Kroll: Kroll's giant octopus-like guardian, believed to be a Druj-fed creature of the Spring realm, was defeated but not slain and was expected to return to hunt when hungry.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: Rebel septs aided by Irra Harah controlled Nesustak Forest. They were fighting the Druj but were no friends of the Empire.

Figure of eight.d: Imperial law on the five religious crimes (abuse of powers, blasphemy, desecration, heresy and idolatry) stays unchanged and remains under the Senate's control. From the end of the Winter Solstice, however, priests stop condemning individuals. Instead they pass proscriptions, which the Constitutional Court scrutinises for constitutionality and clarity. The Tribune was to raise five administrative proscriptions at the summit: excommunication without a writ, dedication to false virtues, the desecration of paragon and exemplar relics, the Excessionist Heresy, and statues of eternals. The Court set out what passing or rejecting each would mean. It also flagged unresolved issues, including the Marcher orcs' heretical belief in reincarnation, fanes, and the Feast of the Broken Wheel.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: raids to free slaves from the Druj are cited as having produced spontaneous auras that appeared Anarchist in nature.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: raids to free slaves from the Grendel are cited as having produced spontaneous auras that appeared Anarchist in nature.
n.Imperial Orcs: Hap the Soft warned the Imperial Orcs assembly that Marcher orcs would face death rather than abandon their beliefs, which conflict with the Doctrine of the Howling Abyss. The magistrates also confirmed that the proposed idolatry proscription would not forbid statues honouring orcs.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher orcs' heretical belief in reincarnation is traced to their Jotun roots.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the true consecration in Holberg is cited as an example of something not protected by the current desecration law.
n.The Marches: The Marcher orcs' belief in reincarnation contradicts the Doctrine of the Howling Abyss, making it heretical. The magistrates deliberately raised no proscription on the matter but warned that the Synod must eventually either outlaw it or implicitly approve it.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: under the current law it would not be illegal to try to destroy the true consecration in Holberg.
t.Mournwold: Hundreds of Marcher orcs living in the Mournwold openly reject a Doctrine of Faith. The Empire has so far looked the other way, but the issue threatens the Synod's moral authority and will have to be settled.

Finding is the final act.d: The Highborn and League Assemblies could enact a mandate creating the lecture Preach Vigilance - Investigate Sarvos; if at least 40 congregations took part, Sentinel Gate opportunities to expose and potentially shut down the ring would follow at the Spring Equinox 388YE, at a cost of four thrones of Sarvos tax for the season. The Sarvosan Chamber of Commerce could vote to send orcs of the College of the Liberated to help, cutting the congregations needed by ten but losing the College's extra money. The Vigilance Assembly could send the Silent Bell to investigate every Bay of Catazar territory for six months. The Whisper Gallery offered an illegal venture to exploit the ring, and Sofia di Sarvos offered weirwood for Bay of Catazar spy networks in exchange for roseweald.

n.Grendel: Grendel spy networks in Sarvos were targeted for exposure and possible dismantling, and the Silent Bell might confirm which Bay of Catazar territories host Grendel agents.
n.Highguard: Joran of Reikos's judgement of peerless kinship meant Highborn congregations could be mandated to travel to Sarvos and help uncover the espionage ring alongside the League.
n.The League: League congregations, the Sarvosan Chamber of Commerce and merchant Sofia di Sarvos were all offered ways to fight the Grendel spies in Sarvos, though the investigation would cost the city four thrones of tax for a season.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: a judgement by Asteria of Ocean Kites Root in the Urizen Assembly helped inspire the Silent Bell's proposed survey of the Bay of Catazar.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Silent Bell could spend six months confirming which Bay of Catazar territories host Grendel agents, and Sofia di Sarvos offered weirwood towards a spy network in an Imperial territory on the Bay.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Joran of Reikos raised the Highborn Assembly judgement calling for peerless kinship with Sarvos.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos was the focus of the effort: congregations could investigate its espionage ring, its Chamber of Commerce would vote on enlisting College of the Liberated orcs, and the disruption would reduce its tax revenue by four thrones for the season.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the espionage ring in Spiral was noted to remain, though damaged by order of the Senate.

Fire and the flood.d: The Boyar's Hasta, Golden Axe, Granite Pillar, Lions of Adelmar and Summer Storm fought under the Druj miasma and the Rivers of Life against the Marshlizard sept and six Druj armies that had slipped from Zenith to the Tower. Five more Druj armies struck Kroll and Turan Flats, forcing the Empire to divide its effort. Nesustak rebels helped, and the Empire won at Turan. At Jarangir's Levy the dam was breached and Imperial lines were scattered. Half the Druj then withdrew south to meet the Shield of Ipotavo, whose bound ghosts aid them. About 2,500 died on each side. A battle opportunity, a Golden Axe transformation and a conjunction followed.

n.Dawn: The Lions of Adelmar shielded their allies from spears and arrows and saved dozens of lives when the levy flooded. Alongside the Summer Storm they drew the Marshlizards' particular hatred.
n.Druj: The Druj lost around 2,500 troops. Their northern counter-attack was driven back into the Salt Flats, and a major force stayed trapped in Thornfen with the Tower weakened but standing. Their septs remained riven by rivalry.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar advanced carefully to spare Highborn lives, then turned north with disciplined resolve to meet the Druj armies out of the Salt Flats.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Summer Storm hunted the Druj with ruthless aggression and took the brunt of casualties at Jarangir's Levy. Soldiers who fought beside them and the Summer champion Murmastis could gain a heroic boon.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the vallorn at Sarangrave's heart is said to threaten worse than the situation in Navarr's Therunin, from which the Druj armies had earlier moved south.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman's Redgate Pass is cited as an earlier pass brought down by the Flasks of Fire and Fury.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Tower of the Skink is compared to the Walls of Holberg and its siege, and Spiral is cited as a place where a mountain pass was blocked.
n.Urizen: Sarangrave was granted to Urizen, but it remained a warzone with only a handful of new spires. The Strategos Lanius was charged with killing Grettek Skinflawed, and five unidentified Urizeni captives awaited rescue.
n.Varushka: The Boyar's Hasta distinguished themselves at Jarangir's Levy. The Golden Axe, fighting beside Ser Gaspare's Summer schlacta, stayed barred from cautious orders but gained a chance to become a Victorious army.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is listed among places where mountain passes have been blocked by sabotage or destructive magic.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; it is linked only through the Dawnish Lions of Adelmar fighting in Sarangrave.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: the Cicatrix Vekor Amberlure is a warden of Cassad Ûln, the mountain fortress in the Forest of Ulnak.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: only the Walls of Holberg are said to surpass the Tower of the Skink, and Holberg's old siege is used as a comparison.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Redgate Pass in Kahraman was brought down by the same Flasks of Fire and Fury that the Druj sought to use.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Five Druj armies led by the Black Wind struck out of the Salt Flats into northern Sarangrave. They were forced back here by season's end, and the trapped Druj hoped to escape here too.
t.Sarangrave: The territory remained a warzone. The Empire made inroads in Thornfen and held the north, while Druj, rebels and a contained vallorn kept its grip fragile and Urizen settlement minimal.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: cited as one of the places where a mountain pass has been blocked by sabotage or magic.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: cited as one of the places where a mountain pass has been blocked by sabotage or magic.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Druj armies that conquered Therunin had moved south, and the Sarangrave vallorn is said to threaten worse than the situation there.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Druj armies had cast down the Stork's Gaze in northern Zenith before an Imperial counter-attack, then escaped under Night magic to the Tower of the Skink.

r.Sarangrave/Bloodwater Marsh: Mentioned in passing: bands of Druj lie hidden here, and the Druj armies fleeing Zenith slipped past Imperial forces in the area.
r.Sarangrave/Kroll: The Druj host out of the Salt Flats pushed into Kroll, where rebels helped Imperial watchposts escape before the Empire drove the invaders back.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: The rebel former slaves and free septs holding the forest, backed by the Prince with a Thousand Foes, harried the northern Druj and warned Imperial soldiers, though they remained no friends of the Empire.
r.Sarangrave/Thornfen: The Empire advanced toward Sephals and the Tower of the Skink and reached three-tenths of the way to conquest. The battle at Jarangir's Levy ended in floods, and the Shield of Ipotavo attacked the Tower from the south.
r.Sarangrave/Turan Flats: The Red Lizard tried to retake Turan at Het Traaka's urging. Days of fighting burned part of the town before the Empire pushed the Druj back.

Flight of birds.d: Guided by the Raven Seer, the mystics found that a new Kallavesi army, which the Senate could authorise at any time, might be relentless, glorious or resourceful. Leofric, following swans into the Sovevann, discovered the ruined Hall of the Soturi. Restoring it would allow one fearless army. Alternatively, a Hall of Names recording Wintermark's named heroes would allow one named army. The two commissions are mutually exclusive. The mystics also asked Wilda, the Wintermark egregore, to call a Witan at the summit so the nation could choose a single Wintermark-relevant problem for them to appraise. They would present at least one opportunity by the following summit.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Fist of the Mountains is said to have died defending Urizen against the depredations of the Grendel.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's lost army gave its lives defending the people of Urizen in Redoubt.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark could raise a new Kallavesi army, gaining the fearless or named quality by commissioning one of two rival halls. The mystics of Ishal also called on the nation to assemble a Witan and choose the problem they should next appraise.

t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa is the source of any new army, drawing on its fearless warriors, foragers and named heroes. A Hall of Names would especially stir the Pride and Loyalty of the often-overlooked Kallavesi.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is where the Fist of the Mountains was destroyed in battle.
t.Tsirku: Mentioned in passing: the mystics confirmed they could investigate Tsirku, as they consider Sydanjaa part of Wintermark's cultural traditions.

r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: The ruined Hall of the Soturi lies deep in the Sovevann here. Either the restored hall or the Hall of Names could be commissioned as an edifice on its site, the former before the end of Autumn Equinox 388YE.

Forever is composed of nows.d: Retired prognosticator Mladen Escovitch offered to work with the Imperial Master of Works to update three existing fortification opportunities, but only if the vacant post is filled and he is engaged during the Winter Solstice. Gerard La Salle proposed hiring a temporary prognosticator, with the Senate choosing by administrative motion between Lisane de Terresford, Rosemary Stockland and Vainakoma Dawnstongue. Alternatively, the Senate could hire all three permanently for 6 extra thrones a season, which would also open a power to review a lapsed opportunity. For a year the Throne may ask Magistrate Abraham and Leontes to appraise a proposed sodality's manifesto. Professor Gelberg's Beurteilung remains available, and Eilian Sweetwater is still missing in Redoubt.

n.Dawn: Lisane de Terresford, a Dawnish earl of House Terresford known for her Wisdom and past work with the Synod, is one of three candidates offered to the Senate as a prognosticator who would seek virtuous solutions.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Mladen Escovitch's freelance work included a recent appraisal of the vulnerabilities of the Druj military.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Eilian Sweetwater vanished during the Grendel attack on Redoubt and may be a prisoner of the Grendel.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the missing prognosticator Eilian Sweetwater is described as a Navarr historian, whose absence prompted the search for a stand-in.
n.The Marches: Rosemary Stockland, an alder of Stockland in Upwold and a former Bailiff of the Grand Market, is offered as a candidate prognosticator who would favour mercantile solutions in which all parties gain.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Eilian Sweetwater and his team disappeared at the fallen Lighthouse at Nikephoros in the Urizen-held territory of Redoubt.
n.Wintermark: Vainakoma Dawnstongue, a Suaq veteran of the Green Shield from Hahnmark, is offered as a candidate prognosticator whose solutions to military problems would make novel use of Imperial armies.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the candidate prognosticator Vainakoma Dawnstongue was born and raised in Hahnmark.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the "Third Pie" opportunity in Mournwold is cited as an example of an earlier opportunity that could be refreshed.
t.Redoubt: Eilian Sweetwater and his team went missing in Redoubt during the Grendel attack, just as they reached the fallen Lighthouse at Nikephoros, and they remain unaccounted for amid rumours involving the eternal Khobel Tavah.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: candidate Lisane de Terresford leads House Terresford, a minor noble house that keeps the ford on the River Terres in Semmerholm.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: candidate Rosemary Stockland is an alder of Stockland, an Upwold region known for its fair and its sheep and cattle markets.

In harmony and unison.d: Grandmaster Elagabala chose the site of Atun's landing for the order's grand lodge. The design centres on an enormous weirwood vessel, proposed name Elagabala's Vision, beside a basilica to the Way and a pier into the Catazar. The commission costs 20 white granite, 15 mithril, 65 weirwood and 300 crowns, with upkeep of 5 thrones. Once built it would add 15 mana crystals to the Conclave font each season, cheapen the Grandmaster's mana, raise congregation investment in Necropolis, let Highguard support one extra navy, and supply true liao each solstice. The Paragon's Voice Chapter and the Black Tablet offered further benefits, conditional on an interdiction and a declaration of concord respectively. The basilica might later be consecrated or expanded into a cathedral.

n.Grendel: The coastal site was acknowledged as an obvious Grendel target, and Elagabala's Vision would be vulnerable to Grendel navies whenever it was at sea, though the Grendel are often loath to destroy valuable things.
n.Highguard: The lodge would celebrate the Highborn role in bringing the Way to the world and their seafaring past, permanently allowing Highguard to raise and support one additional navy once it was built. The vessel could accompany any Highborn navy to give spiritual succour.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: they are not named, though the threat to the Golden Pyramid lodge in Mareave came from the orcs of the Broken Shore.

t.Bay of Catazar: Once complete, Elagabala's Vision could sail along the coast to any Imperial territory on the Bay in a season, but it would be clumsy and vulnerable to attack on these waters. A pier from the lodge would also extend into the Catazar.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: a steward's lesson recalls that the First Empress went on to found the Empire at Anvil in Casinea.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the recently completed Golden Pyramid grand lodge here was briefly threatened by the orcs of the Broken Shore before the Military Council secured it.
t.Necropolis: The territory would host the proposed grand lodge, which would raise the level of investment of every congregation in Necropolis until the vessel sailed elsewhere. The Black Tablet offered to seek a relic from the Necropolis for Whispers through the Black Gate.

r.Mareave/Clisearn: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Pyramid's grand lodge in Clisearn had been protected by the Military Council, which locals cited as reason not to fear for the new site.
r.Necropolis/Coursmouth: Mentioned in passing: the fortress of Reumah's Rest overlooking the cliffs in Coursmouth was cited as reassurance against threats to the coastal site.
r.Necropolis/Sanctuary Sand: Sanctuary, at or just inland from Atun's landing site, was chosen for the planned grand lodge, to the delight of its people. The plans include a basilica to the Way, a pier and a great moored vessel that could evacuate magicians and locals if the region were seriously threatened.

In the ground.d: Adamant's herald Meon of the Chisel answered Stone Smith Gemma Brightsmith. All his aid depends on the Senate recommissioning Eastern Guard in Upwold or conceding it to him. If that is settled, he offers to raise Farstrider's Watch to an unbreakable rank-three fortification, to build an unsinkable Hall of the Kingfisher at Fisher's Rock with optional marsh-draining dykes, and to raise a sealed dolmen weakening curses on the Mournwold. All must be commissioned by the Autumn Equinox 388YE, and a Ring of the Dragon schema is offered for ilium. Tharim's knights compensated farmers for damage with Heart's Blood, and his herald Poena offered landskeepers blades, Bitter Salt and a savage army enchantment. Sadogua offered mushroom elixirs and masks to mummers.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Adamant Gate in eastern Semmerholm is cited as the standard of unbreakability for the proposed Hall of the Kingfisher.
n.Jotun: The Jotun hold Bregasland, where Adamant offers to build a fortress regardless, and they are advancing across Mitwold. Several of Tharim's boons are expected to be turned against them, and some smiths worry because Adamant has aided the Jotun in the past.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: plans for curse wards drawn up by Richard of Holberg are dismissed by Adamant's herald as relying on less reliable magics.
n.The Marches: Marcher smiths, landskeepers and mummers were each courted by a different eternal, gaining offers of great fortifications, curse wards, military enchantments and magical gifts. Much of this depends first on resolving the fate of Eastern Guard.

t.Bregasland: Although the territory is held by the Jotun, Adamant offers to help carve an unbreakable, unsinkable Hall of the Kingfisher from Fisher's Rock. Dykes could be added that would raise farm investment, and the keep could become a shrine to Loyalty honouring Bolstering Bill.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Richard of Holberg's curse ward plans are rejected by Adamant's herald.
t.Mitwold: Tharim's knights damaged Mitwold farms while hunting Agramant's servants, and the Bound King paid compensation in Heart's Blood. The Jotun are advancing across the territory, and Tharim suggests his Bitter Salt boon could help garrison Forte Fidelis.
t.Mournwold: Adamant offers to make Farstrider's Watch a majestic, unbreakable castle and to raise a sealed dolmen that would weaken curses on the territory, though its mana sites would yield bronze dragonseyes in place of some crystal mana. Sadogua's heralds flocked especially to the Mournwold's Wassail.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the Adamant Gate in eastern Semmerholm is used as a comparison for the unbreakable keep Adamant proposes.
t.Upwold: Adamant's herald met the smiths at the Woldstone and made all aid conditional on the decommissioned Eastern Guard being recommissioned or ceded to him. Tharim's knights remain camped here, and his herald Poena visited the Silent Giant seeking the landskeepers.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: Adamant proposes dykes and bulwarks connected to the Hall of the Kingfisher to drain parts of the fens. This would remove the marsh quality while leaving fens in place, and the keep would remain safe even if the sea drowned the region.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Farstrider's Watch here could be improved to a rank-three fortification infused with adamant, partly paid for in weltsilver and orichalcum. It could also be consecrated to Pride with a shrine to the Ore Hills Rebels.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: A ring of sealed dolmen could be built in the western Ore Hills with Adamant's aid to weaken curses affecting the Mournwold, at the cost of altered mana production across the territory.

Invited with asperity.d: Rak Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragons-Undivided, who plans to retire, was to attend the Senate with potential successors to celebrate the five-year peace treaty and discuss the Druj, the vallorn and the Jotun. The skuldyr invited Imperial storytellers to Leopard-Tooth Pass. The Dragons refused to allow a sea route to Otkodov. Thule forces moved into Ossium's woods, and Tathenon the Gyre invited Imperial warbands and armies to join an assault on the Forest of Ulnak. Caridis offered Varushkans a joint raid on the trudnik face-peelers, which would cast suspicion on the draughir. Thule warlocks at the Icy Crag sought ritual texts, Fraynir sought Dreadful Ending, and Orobus offered ilium for living weirwood trees.

n.Druj: The Thule were preparing to invade the Druj-held Forest of Ulnak after their hunters scouted it, and they invited Imperial warbands and armies to join the assault.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of Skarsind are said to keep the Thule at arm's length where possible.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the ever-present Jotun in the west were listed among the topics for Rak's state visit.
n.Navarr: Navarr was sending food north to Otkodov, and Navarri bards were invited to the storytelling exchange. The Thule also asked for advance warning before the trods network is completed, and Orobus offered ilium for living weirwood trees from Hercynia or Miaren.
n.Thule: The Dragons sent Rak and his possible successors to Anvil, refused an Imperial sea route, moved armies into Ossium and towards Ulnak, and placed warlocks at the Icy Crag. They also sought Imperial rituals and weirwood trees to prepare Sküld against its vallorn.
n.Varushka: Varushka, the nation most critical of the peace, was offered a joint raid with the Claws of the Dragon against the trudnik in Karsk and Ossium, with the Boyar's Hasta able to support it. Any attack on the trudnik would unsettle the nation's draughir.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark scops were invited to exchange tales with the skuldyr at Leopard-Tooth Pass. The page also notes quiet Wintermark grumbling about the Empire surrendering land to the northern orcs.

t.Forest of Ulnak: Thule hunters scouted the forest through the Imperial spy network ahead of a planned Thule invasion. Imperial warbands joining it were promised crystal mana, and armies were welcome if their generals accepted Tathenon the Gyre's strategy, with a risk of clashes if they did not.
t.Hercynia: Orobus offered 12 rings of ilium for living trees from the Heartwood of the Great Vale, which would permanently cut its weirwood production by 1 wain a season. The decision fell to whoever won the seat at auction.
t.Karsk: Tasya of the Black Feathers, envoy of the Charnel Lord, visited the Thule fortification of Krevsatyzmei here. Karsk was also a target of the proposed face-peeler raid, which would bring a production penalty to its draughir.
t.Miaren: Orobus offered 12 rings of ilium for living trees from the Golden Trees of Seren, which would permanently reduce their weirwood production by 1 wain a season, if the seat's holder agreed.
t.Miekarova: Thule warlocks led by Thania of the Blackstaff took up residence at the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, cutting its upkeep by five thrones a season. Thania offered mithril or golden apples for certain ritual texts.
t.Ossium: Thule forces moved into the Bonewood and Webwood, and Ossium was the main target of the proposed raid on the trudnik, with the Boyar's Hasta able to support it from here. The raid would cost Ossium's draughir a production penalty.
t.Otkodov: The Thule homeland was due to receive Imperial storytellers at Leopard-Tooth Pass, while the Dragons refused any Imperial sea route or trading post on its coast. Food from the Marches and Navarr continued to flow north to feed its people and armies.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Mentioned in passing: Imperial fighting along its border was said to help the Thule goals in Ulnak.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's campaign to conquer Sarangrave was said to aid the Thule even without direct support in Ulnak.
t.Sea of Snow: An Imperial proposal to map its northern waters and find a passage to Otkodov's coast was rejected. The Thule cited terrible beasts in the ice-strewn seas, and plainly did not want Imperial fleets near their shores.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the Thule recalled fighting alongside the Empire to liberate Sermersuaq.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs of Skarsind are said to keep the Thule at arm's length.
t.Tsirku: Mentioned in passing: Rak cited a recent overland trade route attempt through the wastes of Tsirku as an unmitigated disaster that cost many lives.

r.Ossium/Bonewood: Thule forces entered the Bonewood, which had been woven with Spring magic so that its trees attack intruders. Orobus also hoped to transplant weirwood that 'remembers' the vallorn to share with the trees of the Bonewood.
r.Ossium/Webwood: Thule forces entered the Spring-warded Webwood, a known haunt of the face-peelers. Under Caridis's terms, any trudnik spoils from Slomavetka, a lair just across the border here, would go to the Thule.
r.Otkodov/Nithoggir: The Dragons refused to cooperate in finding a sea passage to the coast of Nithoggir and would not permit an Imperial trading post there.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: The Thule were building rings of warded white granite stones around the vallorn at Emrys and asked for a season's warning before the vallorn's transformation. Imperial storytellers were invited to Leopard-Tooth Pass in Kógur.

Mermaids in the basement.d: Lutomysla found the bridges would cost over three thousand wains of white granite, would need engineering the Empire lacks, and would not remove the island quality. She offered several alternatives. Dedicated berths could let the Red Wind Corsairs cross freely. A fane to Janon could do the same for the Burning Falcon. Lashonar's songbirds could summon the corsair families to defend the islands, and Azoth's Archipelago Parador could end the Cazar Straits' poverty. Khobel Tavah might sink the islands entirely. New shipyards at Elos, Atalaya or Oran could support a navy. Of these, only the Red Wind Wharfs were later built, being commissioned in Summer 388YE.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Causeway that carried Dawn's armies across the Semmerlak was cited as a magical precedent unlikely to be repeated.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj were named as the enemy the Golden Causeway was created to fight, and as a far greater threat than the Wreckers.
n.Grendel: The Grendel were named as a key obstacle, as they hold the Elos docks, smash bridges, have destroyed the shipyards at Atalaya and control the seas with their armada. Lutomysla judged that they fear an Imperial navy more than anything.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard was listed among the nations already supporting as many forces as they can.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn were offered several ways to reach their islands: berths for the Red Wind Corsairs, a fane to Janon for the Burning Falcon, corsair defence through Lashonar's songbirds, the Archipelago Parador, and a new navy rallied around the prow of the Storm's Child. Only the Red Wind Wharfs were later built.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: League engineers of Temeschwar and Holberg rejected the idea of undersea tunnels, and the League was noted as soon to be at its force limit.
n.Urizen: Urizen was noted to have an existing opportunity to support a navy alongside its two armies. This would require reclaiming Elos intact and building the Cargo Cranes.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the prognosticator Lutomysla Niegoslava who led the appraisal is Varushkan.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: expanding Oran's wharfs was said to secure Oran as a crucial port on the Bay, and every nation adjoining it was said to be at its force limit.
t.Feroz: Feroz's Cazar Straits, held by the Iron Confederacy, was assessed for bridges, berths and corsair defence, and was offered the Archipelago Parador to end its poverty. The Red Wind berths at Oran were later built.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the walls and pumps of Holberg were invoked as comparisons for the scale of the problem.
t.Madruga: Madruga's Free Landing remained in Wrecker hands. It was proposed as the site for a fane to Janon and a rebuilt Atalaya shipyard, and Lightsea was proposed as the home of the songbird defence.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium was named as the land Dawn invaded via the Golden Causeway.
t.Redoubt: Expanding the Elos docks into a shipyard was offered, but Elos was in Grendel hands, so nothing could be done until it was reclaimed.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos's island bridges and the Spider's Tollkeep were cited as far smaller precedents.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Semmerholm was not named directly, but the Golden Causeway that Dawn's armies used was cited as an example of eternal aid.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar's mining professors dismissed undersea tunnels as impossible, and a Temeschwar academic appears in the in-character fiction.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Causeway across the Semmerlak was cited as a precedent for eternal-built crossings.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The Straits, controlled by the Iron Confederacy and impoverished by Rahab's rule, could have that poverty lifted by the Archipelago Parador. The region would also be covered by the berths and corsair defence proposals.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: New berths at Oran would let the Red Wind Corsairs cross to the Cazar Straits freely, and these were commissioned in Summer 388YE. A costlier expansion of the wharfs into a full shipyard was also offered.
r.Madruga/Crucible: Mentioned in passing: 'Crucible' appears only as a title of the eternal Azoth, not in reference to the region.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Free Landing, still held by the Children of Wrecks, was proposed as the site for Janon's Alcazar of Flame and a rebuilt Atalaya shipyard, though neither was built.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: Quzar in Lightsea was named as the location for the Song of Salt and Sand. Through it, Lashonar's songbirds could call the corsairs to defend the islands, but Lashonar was not approached.
r.Redoubt/Naris: The Elos docks in Naris could be cheaply expanded into a shipyard, but only once they were reclaimed from the Grendel.

Mirror and the flame.d: The Tribunal appointed Alexius as Ambassador to the Empire, asked the Empire to reciprocate and suggested neither side build an embassy. It announced a fane to Sinokenon that would take at least a year; an Imperial ambassador could try to coerce them to drop it, at diplomatic cost. Through its herald, Sinokenon offered a magnitude 120 ritual stronger than Clarity of the Master Strategist in return for Silver Flame access to Imperial lore, and a ritual adding five ranks to a military unit for a 60-throne Senate offer. It also offered a Circlet of Supreme Authority to Emperor Vesna. Oblivion Sentinel Floria Sunshaper was made responsible for defeating the Grendel and their Asavean companions.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named among those who have invaded Spiral in the past.
n.Grendel: A Grendel company escorting Asaveans carrying shards of Black Plateau glass was trying to reach a ship in Apulus, and Floria Sunshaper was charged with defeating them; the Silver Flame also said they would not trade with the Grendel out of respect for the Empire.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Spiral's assignment to the League is recalled as the cause of the Urizeni rebellion, and the League city of Apulian is noted for its explosive growth since the rebellion was settled.
n.Urizen: The rebels who formed the Tribunal still embody Urizeni culture but have mostly severed their bond with Menos, and their offer of access to Urizeni lore proved impossible because Urizen magically means only the nation within the Empire; Urizen's senators had earlier chosen to receive Silver Flame foci under the peace settlement.

t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that the Grendel's main focus remains on Redoubt and Mareave.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the page notes that the Grendel's main focus remains on Redoubt and Mareave.
t.Spiral: Spiral now contains a self-declared independent Tribunal in Cinion that plans a fane to Sinokenon inside an Imperial territory, while a Grendel and Asavean party threatened to carry Black Plateau glass out of the territory.

r.Spiral/Apulus: Grendel escorting Asaveans with shards of volcanic glass were heading for a ship in a sheltered cove in Apulus, posing a threat to the Black Plateau that Floria Sunshaper was charged with ending.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Cinion, ruled by the rebels, became the seat of the Tribunal of the Silver Flame, which planned a fane to Sinokenon there that could bring as many heralds into the region as there are Urizeni.

Mushroom, mushroom, mushroom.d: Llofir accepted neutrality as a compromise but refused any favours to the nations it blames for destroying its Tamarbode garden. Its heralds sought a Navarr-only meeting through Advisor on the Vallorn Seren Embercast. They offered scouring support for a new army in Miaren and up to 15 wains of mithril-equivalent equipment in exchange for 1,000 herbs. They also proposed Llofir's Paludarium in Greenfalls. Llofir urged casting Hallow of the Green World on the Druj through conjoined conjunctions to Eastring, where Druj ghulai sought to rile the vallorn, although an interdiction made this illegal. The Paludarium was not built and Hallow was not cast. Regrow the Land's Heart enhanced with Llofir's power was cast on Hahnmark and Ossium.

n.Druj: Llofir judged the Druj to be in decline and proposed Hallow of the Green World in Therunin to bring sickness and ruin upon them, while Druj ghulai at Eastring tried to rile the vallorn further. The ritual was never cast on them.
n.Highguard: Llofir still blames Highguard for destroying its Tamarbode garden and offered it no favours or assistance. Casting Regrow the Land's Heart with Llofir's power on a Highborn territory would invite vengeance, but might also ease the eternal's anger.
n.Navarr: The Navarr were singled out for Llofir's aid. It offered scouring support and mycelial arms for a new army in Miaren and proposed a garden in Greenfalls. In Summer 388YE the Senate commissioned that army with Llofir's help.
n.The League: Llofir counts the League among those responsible for its garden's destruction, denies it any aid, and openly welcomes anyone willing to bring it to account.
n.Urizen: Llofir continues to hold Urizen to account for the Tamarbode garden and refuses it favours. It warned that Regrow the Land's Heart cast with its power on an Urizen territory would provoke vengeance, though this might also repair relations.
n.Varushka: Ossium received Regrow the Land's Heart infused with Llofir's power, so its farms and herb gardens yielded magical mushrooms for the following season.
n.Wintermark: Hahnmark received Regrow the Land's Heart infused with Llofir's power, so its farms and herb gardens yielded magical mushrooms for the following season.

t.Brocéliande: Heralds of Llofir appeared here after the Autumn Equinox to talk with Navarr magicians and vates about the war against the vallorn.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Had Hallow of the Green World been cast on the Druj, its effects would have concentrated here and freed Spring eternals to act. The ritual was not performed.
t.Hahnmark: Regrow the Land's Heart was cast here with Llofir's power, so its farms and herb gardens produced magical mushrooms for the following season.
t.Hercynia: Heralds of Llofir visited Hercynia to speak with Navarr magicians and vates about aiding the fight against the vallorn.
t.Miaren: Llofir offered to support the new Navarr army raised in Miaren if it was dedicated to destroying the vallorn. It also proposed a garden at Greenfalls, which was never commissioned.
t.Ossium: Regrow the Land's Heart was cast here with Llofir's power, so its farms and herb gardens produced magical mushrooms for the following season.
t.Reikos: Llofir's original garden here was destroyed, the source of its grudge against Highguard, the League and Urizen. The eternal's earlier scouring of Reikos had erased Druj scars along with much Highborn history.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: This was one of the Druj territories where Hallow of the Green World would have concentrated and freed Spring eternals to act, but the ritual was not cast.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: its vallorn heart is one of only two not yet linked to the trod network in the Navarr plan to render the vallorn mortal.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: it lies dangerously close to the proposed garden site at Greenfalls, though Llofir believed it could repel any attack.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: it lies dangerously close to the proposed garden site at Greenfalls, though Llofir believed it could repel any attack.
t.Therunin: Druj ghulai sought to rile the vallorn here, threatening further expansion, and the territory was the proposed casting site for Hallow of the Green World. That ritual would have weakened the vallorn and transformed the land, but it was not cast.

r.Miaren/Greenfalls: Llofir chose Greenfalls for a new garden, Llofir's Paludarium, which would have consumed the region and its Navarr ruins. It was never commissioned.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Llofir's former garden at Tamarbode was destroyed, and that loss is the root of the eternal's lingering grudge.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Conjoined conjunctions opened to Greensward Lea in Eastring, where Druj ghulai sought to rile the vallorn. Securing the site would have allowed a ritual team to cast Hallow of the Green World.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: Had Hallow of the Green World been cast, this region would have lost its poisoned quality and gained the Mycelial quality. The ritual was not performed.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Had Hallow of the Green World been cast, Peakedge Song would have become forested as Llofir swept away its ruins. The ritual was not performed.
r.Therunin/Upper Tarn Valley: Had Hallow of the Green World been cast, the Upper Tarn Valley would have become forested as Llofir swept away its ruins. The ritual was not performed.

My friends are my estate.d: Senator Genoveva Barossa d'Apulian's appraisal sent Naomi to Spiral. She proposed five options. The Obsidian Shipwrights great work would protect fleets from the Plateau, aid scouting and Sarcophan trade, harm Sumaah and Commonwealth trade, and add taxes; it could include a giant Sailor or Witch statue to rival the Colossus of Sarvos. The Palace of Mists would raise Apulian to a rank-two fortification and hamper seaborne attacks. Swords Against Darkness would be a questing venture, needing League and Urizen statements of principle. The Northern Way would link Apulian to Zenith and could expand the Crucible of Fate. A revised Oblivion's Edge would enclose the Black Plateau. All remain proposals.

n.Dawn: Dawnish military units could join the proposed Swords Against Darkness quest in Spiral alongside League and Urizen units, as their glory hunters are thought impossible to keep away.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: remnants of Druj insurgents lurk in Spiral's wilds, and Oblivion's Edge is meant partly to deter Druj raids on the Black Plateau.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel remnants hide in Spiral, the Grendel attack on Elos is cited as a maritime threat, and their old highways towards the Legacy would form the base of the Northern Way.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highborn vessels are among the ships now seen entering Apulian's harbour.
n.The League: League engineers, guilds and merchants are central to every proposal. Success could make Apulian a rival to Sarvos, and League artisans might be invited to learn ushabti-making at the Crucible of Fate.
n.Urizen: Urizen seers, architects and spires would share in the proposals. The Urizen Assembly's statements could unlock the venture and cheapen the Northern Way, and Urizen fleets, businesses and spires in Spiral would benefit.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: crossing the bay by sail was once preferred to overland travel, and a night crossing in a converted bumboat proved the shipwrights' protective enchantments.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: listed among the four older League cities whose centuries of history Apulian is measured against.
t.Mareave: Mentioned in passing: Curstag's Way already links Mareave to the Empire, and the Northern Way might benefit the orcs there too.
t.Morrow: If the Northern Way is built and League artisans join the Crucible, Urizen or League characters with resources in Morrow could have them upgraded with bespoke ushabti.
t.Redoubt: The Brilliant Star's output could fall by three wains if Crucible ushabti were diverted to the Legacy, or keep its support if League artisans doubled the Crucible's capacity. Resources here could also become eligible for upgrades.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Apulian's ambitions are framed as rivalry with Sarvos and its Colossus, and the Great Chain of Sarvos inspired the Palace of Mists.
t.Spiral: The territory would gain from any of these proposals: fewer Black Plateau penalties on fleets, businesses and military units, higher taxation, stronger defences, and a fortification enclosing the Plateau.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is named among the older League cities, and the shipwrights' method was co-developed by Danilo di Tassato.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Apulian is compared with Temeschwar as a League city blending another nation's wisdom with League ambition.
t.Zenith: The proposed Northern Way would raise investment in Zenith's businesses by one level and connect its spires and the Crucible of Fate to Apulian's trade.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Mentioned in passing: Beoraidh is noted as a new Sarcophan protectorate south of Spiral, and one of its merchants backed the shipping talks.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: Mentioned in passing: the Great Chain of Sarvos, which guards Cigno against shore offensives, inspired the proposed Apulian defences.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: The proposed Northern Way would run through Apstrus, carrying trade between Apulian and Zenith with protected stopping places.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Apulus would host the proposed Obsidian Shipwrights and Palace of Mists. Seaborne attackers there would face a 20% penalty, and the region could gain a giant statue rivalling the Colossus.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: The Northern Way would pass through Ossuary on its route from Apulian towards the Twilight Gate and Zenith.
r.Spiral/Screed: Oblivion's Edge, a proposed level-one fortification, would enclose the Black Plateau in Screed. It would stop a single season of fighting from rousing the Plateau and require 20 victory points to capture the region.
r.Zenith/Proceris: The Northern Way would climb through the Twilight Gate into Proceris to join the Bridge of the Sky between the Golden Cascade farms and the Crucible of Fate.

Ourselves and immortality.d: Prospero granted Vossk of Zenith Ascendant a parley and called in the favour owed by the Celestial Arch. Siakha agreed to discuss destruction with Ibiss Briarheart and gave three new rituals to Urizen lore. The Thrice-cursed Court accepted a midnight parley, invited the Keeper of Tharim's Throne, and Surut demanded tribute from warriors. Ylenwe said the Kronemark Sungate cannot be closed, proposed a hall of music in Skarsind and urged aid for the Commonwealth and Jarm against Cold Sun. The Whisper Gallery set a masked-only parley in the Hall of Worlds. Adamant offered the Throne of the Mountains ritual in return for wider building powers for four Imperial titles.

n.Dawn: The Keeper of Tharim's Throne, Claudia Varkulova Remislav, was invited as the King-in-Chains' guest at the Thrice-cursed parley. The Court also said that Armand Remislav Who Was Remys remains beloved of them but will not be given Unleash Wild Fire.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Siakha's tempest declared there would be no talk of Grendel or wreckers at her parley.
n.Imperial Orcs: Ylenwe proposed an edifice in the White Wood of Skarsind, the Harmonious Hall, which would have to be ceded to the eternal. Her herald will discuss it with the Archmage of Day, Skywise Gralka, and the High Bard.
n.The League: The Whisper Gallery's parley singled out several invitees, including Archmage of Night Bella Vicente d'Apulian, Senator for Spiral Genoveva Barossa d'Apulian and Custodian of Legacy Rafael Barossa d'Apulian.
n.Urizen: Siakha placed three new rituals in Urizen lore as a gift requested by Ibiss Briarheart. Vossk of Zenith Ascendant was summoned to parley with Prospero, who wants the Celestial Arch to repay its favour.
n.Varushka: Adamant welcomed more white granite fortresses in northern Varushka but refused to make them cheaper, saying the Vorazi do not see the bigger picture.
n.Wintermark: Ylenwe declared the Sungate in Kronemark an open wound sustained by the Oblivion Flame, beyond her power to close. For now it can only be avoided.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the page names no event there, though the Thrice-cursed parley will touch on the Keeper of Tharim's Throne, knights, regio and the vallorn.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the robe of Siakha's tempest herald is described as evoking the wind-tossed breakers of the Bay of Catazar.
t.Hahnmark: Ylenwe confirmed that the Sungate in Hahnmark's Kronemark cannot be closed and that mortals cannot approach it, unless fate changes in future.
t.Skarsind: Ylenwe proposed building the Harmonious Hall in the White Wood. It would cost 15 weirwood, 10 mithril, 10 ilium and 75 crowns, must be ceded to her, and its effects are still unclear.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Genoveva Barossa d'Apulian, Senator for Spiral, is among those the Whisper Gallery invited to its parley.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the page describes no events in Temeschwar itself.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Archmage of Autumn summoned by Prospero is Vossk of Zenith Ascendant.

r.Hahnmark/Kronemark: The Sungate in Kronemark is fed directly by the fury of the Oblivion Flame. Ylenwe cannot close it or let mortals near it, so it must simply be avoided.

Poets light but lamps.d: Cinder zealots attacked the docks at Fisk and Meade and the Azure Chorus. The Fisk attack was contained, but both others turned bloody. Faraden condemned the attacks, shared intelligence, and conjunctions opened to stop further attacks in Sarvos, Madruga and Upwold. Faraden proposed that the Empire attack Ribeira and Pedreira while the Suranni struck southern Reinos, and the Sansar offered a Moonsong Market in the Barrens. The Iron Confederacy took the Cazar Straits from the Children of Wrecks and threatened Free Landing. Sumaah white granite awaits an escort, and the Frieøyer helped complete the Zemress Academy's work. Tsark offered two gardens, and Skoura offered troops for dragonbone.

n.Dawn: Faraden merchants of the Sansar family offered a Moonsong Market in the Barrens, trading Dawnish wine and cloth for Faraden mooncheese and cloth, overseen by a Moonsong Reeve whose benefits are halved if the post is not held by yeofolk.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Faraden declined the Imperial suggestion that its troops might fight the Druj, citing distance and danger.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: named as the foe that Skouran war-engineers could help resist at Rucraic's Redoubt, as former conquerors of the Cazar Straits, and as a naval benchmark.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Accalon of Highguard is the Sumaah ambassador, and the Basilica of Seven Doors is used as a comparison for the Faraden Temple of the High Flames.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skoura wishes to deal mainly with the Unshackled, and its Geltcourse Trade Security Council seeks wider trade only if the Artisans Guild becomes an Imperial sodality. It also offered 500 war-engineers for Rucraic's Redoubt in return for 50 dragonbone.
