n.Jotun: Faraden proposed an Imperial attack on Ribeira and Pedreira alongside a Suranni assault on southern Reinos. At Meade, the Jotun fought the Cinders beside the Marchers, drowned the three captured attackers and restored the docks, adding an idol of Skjaldir.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: northern Hercynia is named as a possible alpine site for future zaboravi gardens.
n.The Brass Coast: Cinders massacred pilgrims at the Azure Chorus before Freeborn and Faraden stormed the Parador together, and Cinders now threaten the House of Guerra. The Suranni hold the Cazar Straits but let Freeborn leave freely, Sumaah granite awaits an escort, and the Zemress Academy has completed its work.
n.The League: Cinders are marching on the Anvil Library Scriptorium in Sarvos, which the Armarius Ricardo Glostari di Sarvos must defend, and the Suranni commended Senator Laurencio Lemmini di Sarvos.
n.The Marches: The Cinders struck the docks at Meade, where Marchers and Jotun fought them together, and more Cinders aim at Benson's Orchard in Upwold. Ebenezer of the Marches, as ambassador, secured Faraden intelligence on the sect.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are listed among the nations with an Imperial ambassador, and the orcs of Otkodov are covered elsewhere.
n.Urizen: Tsark proposed the Garden of the Perfect World in Occursion, a ministry overseen by a Seeker of the Perfect World chosen by the Urizen National Assembly to trade white granite for weirwood and liao. Tsark is also curious about ushabti and the Golden Cascade.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: northern Varushka is named as a possible alpine site for future zaboravi gardens.
n.Wintermark: Tsark offered to help Wintermark cultivate zaboravi through the Garden of Peaceful Quietude sinecure. Warnings about the Cinders were also carried there, and the scholar Marko Siwarsbairn remains in the Iron Confederacy.

t.Bay of Catazar: Some of the Wreckers driven from the Cazar Straits quit the Bay altogether. Suranni control of the Straits could in principle cut Feroz off from the Bay, and Sumaah granite awaits an escort across these waters.
t.Feroz: The Iron Confederacy drove the Children of Wrecks from the Cazar Straits and claims them by conquest. It lets Freeborn leave and Ferozi ships pass, and its merchants eye Bramar once trade routes severed by disaster are restored.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: northern Hercynia is noted as potentially suitable for a zaboravi garden after an appraisal.
t.Kahraman: The Freeborn Assembly warned of a planned attack here, and Cinder pilgrims massacred people in the Parador of Wind and Flame at the Azure Chorus before Freeborn and Faraden stormed it together.
t.Kalino: Known to the Suranni as Arbonne, Kalino suffered a second, far worse curse of ruined crops, sickness and demonic revenants. Its Duke's position is shaky, and Veiled Shrine priests blame Imperial involvement.
t.Madruga: Cinders seek to destroy the House of Guerra in Calvos, and the Iron Confederacy plans to attack the Wreckers in Free Landing after the Spring Equinox if the Empire has not dealt with them. A Frieøyer ship also arrived at Calvos.
t.Mareave: Skoura's Delvemistress wrote to Mareave seeking to deal mainly with its Unshackled neighbours, weighing an embassy and trade. She also offered war-engineers to help defend Rucraic's Redoubt against the Grendel.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Tsark, still refusing an embassy, proposed limited trade through a garden ministry in Zenith and offered to help cultivate zaboravi in the Empire.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: relations with the orcs of Otkodov are noted as covered in another wind of fortune.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the name appears only in Rucraic's Redoubt, the Unshackled fortification Skoura offered to reinforce.
t.Reinos: Faraden proposed that the Empire attack Ribeira and Pedreira after the Winter Solstice while the Iron Confederacy attacks the south, catching the Jotun between hammer and anvil.
t.Sarvos: Cinders are approaching the Anvil Library Scriptorium to burn its books, and a conjunction lets heroes intercept them. War also rages in the seas off Sarvos.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: its dangers make overland trade with the Empire more attractive to Faraden merchants than seaborne trade with Asavea.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Faraden argued that taking Pedreira would protect Segura's western border from future Jotun invasion.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial ambassador told the Suranni that the Empire intends to attack Skallahn.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is named as a possible alpine location for a future zaboravi garden.
t.The Barrens: The Sansar proposed building the Moonsong Market here, a great work that would raise farm investment and draw more Faraden trade and visitors to Dawn.
t.Upwold: Cinders plan to desecrate Benson's Orchard, the Vigilance memorial whose pilgrims stand ready to defend it, and a conjunction lets heroes stop them first.
t.Veroigne: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni ambassador's seat at Chaubrette is said to lie west of Veroigne.
t.Zenith: Tsark proposed the Garden of the Perfect World in Occursion as a trading ministry, and expressed interest in the Golden Cascade that feeds Zenith.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Two Suranni armies carried by the Wings of Kobol smashed the Children of Wrecks here. The Iron Confederacy now claims the islands by right of conquest while inviting trapped Freeborn to leave.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the page refers only to Feroz generally, the town of Bramar and severed trade routes.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: Cinders heading for the House of Guerra can be intercepted along the Corsair's Road, under the responsibility of the Hand of Guerra, Sufyan i Zuhri i Guerra.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Most of the Wreckers fleeing the Cazar Straits went to Free Landing. The Suranni Dukes intend to attack it after the Spring Equinox, and to keep it, unless the Empire acts first.
r.Reinos/Pedreira: Faraden proposed an Imperial attack here after the Winter Solstice, noting it would give the Empire the white granite quarry at Cantera Balanka and shield Segura.
r.Reinos/Ribeira: Faraden urged the Military Council to send a powerful force to take this region after the Winter Solstice in concert with the Suranni attack in the south.
r.Sarvos/Foracci: The main group of Cinders is approaching along Vintner's Way, where the Armarius of the Anvil Library must cut them off.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Dawnguard is one of the two sites the Sansar requested for the proposed Moonsong Market, being close to well-defended centres.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Murderdale is one of the two sites the Sansar requested for the proposed Moonsong Market.
r.Upwold/Tower March: The Cinders must pass through Benson's Bawn to reach Benson's Orchard, and Martin Orchard is responsible for stopping them there.
r.Zenith/Occursion: The foothills of Occursion are the proposed site of Tsark's Garden of the Perfect World, a meditative garden and meeting hall serving as a trading ministry.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; Zenith appears only through the Occursion garden and the Golden Cascade.

Quietude.d: Anka Karass identified two sept members who revealed the Last Battle's location to the Druj and expected the Empire to execute them. Imperial law does not make it a crime for foreigners to aid the Empire's enemies, so the Envoy to the Karass had to tell her at the Execution Field in the Bleaks that she must free them. Knights-errant of House Courcillon were goading the Karass, and Dawnish troubadours' poetry outreach was angrily rebuffed. Anka again asked for the wayhouse to be moved. The Hearth Hearted's enchantment aided Dawn, Navarr, the Great Forest Orcs and the Rahvin, but not the Karass. The Great Forest Orcs completed the Fastness of Thorns, proposed a Navarr Broker of Thorns receiving 11 wains of weirwood, and gifted Lady Renata a wain of weirwood.

n.Dawn: Dawnish settlers gained prosperity from the Hearth Hearted enchantment and the Great Forest Orcs answered Renata's Gift with a wain of weirwood, but House Courcillon's knights-errant and the troubadours' poetry outreach inflamed the Karass.
n.Druj: Druj influence over the Barrens is ebbing. Their recent attack on the Last Battle relied on information from two Karass, whom Anka Karass has now handed over.
n.Navarr: The Navarr benefited from the Autumn enchantment and faced Karass demands to move the Last Battle. The Great Forest Orcs offered them a proposed Broker of Thorns seat receiving 11 wains of weirwood a season, in return for aid if the Eaves of Peytaht are threatened.

t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the remnants of the Black Wind are said to have fled alongside the Druj after a failed invasion of the Sarangrave.
t.The Barrens: The territory grew quieter and more Dawnish as an Autumn enchantment spread prosperity among those with dominion there. Tensions with the Karass festered while the Great Forest Orcs and Rahvin grew stronger.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: refugees from Therunin have gathered at the Last Battle wayhouse and among the Great Forest Orcs in the Barrens.

r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Aided by the Autumn enchantment, the Rahvin made significant progress mustering and arming an army with Fangs mithril. They pointedly ignored the Dawnish apart from a complaint that stolen mithril has not been returned.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The Great Forest Orcs completed the weirwood Fastness of Thorns, sheltered thriving communities of refugees and offered weirwood to the Navarr and Rahvin. They also sent a gift of weirwood to Lady Renata.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Mentioned in passing: survivors of the destruction of Hope's Rest now live in the Heart of Peytaht, where the Great Forest Orcs keep them apart from the Therunin refugees.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: The Last Battle wayhouse, attacked by the Druj, remains a grievance for the Karass, who also face harassment there by Courcillon knights-errant. Anka Karass waits with the accused pair at the Execution Field.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: The Karass live scattered here, and the Earl of the Groves is rumoured to be making mysterious preparations in his manse at the heart of the Groves.

Rebuild Great Library of Ankarien.d: Proposed by the senator for Redoubt and seconded by Miaren's senator, the motion commissioned an edifice costing thirty wains of white granite and 90 crowns in labour, taking three months to complete. Funding came from several citizens after the Winter Solstice 387YE, led by Fausta Ankarien with 9 thrones 4 crowns, alongside smaller donations from Eleri Bronwen's Rest, Bakar i Riqueza and others. The thirty wains of white granite were finally supplied by Spyridonakes of the Lighthouse-That-Was after the Autumn Equinox 388YE. Once complete, the ruins of Ankarien are to be restored to their former glory.

n.The League: The League sees a long-held promise kept, as the Great Library of Ankarien is rebuilt in its Spiral homeland, with Fausta Ankarien foremost among its funders.

t.Spiral: Spiral, held by the League, is to gain the restored Great Library of Ankarien, rebuilt on its original site.

r.Spiral/Ankra: Ankra is the site of the rebuilt Great Library, which on completion will restore the ruins of Ankarien to their former glory.

Red skies.d: The Gathered Storm set a trap for the Red Wind Corsairs off Trivento but was flanked by Imperial captains, many bolstered by Summer magic, and routed. General Joaquim i Erigo's Corsairs pursued them into Madruga and destroyed them in a bloody battle in Calvos Sound, losing under four hundred sailors and capturing the Storm's Child with the stolen Freeborn Storm figurehead, later given to the Freeborn egregores. The Children of Wrecks still hold Free Landing behind Siakha's maelstrom. The Iron Confederacy's Wings of Kobol conquered the Cazar Straits, executing Wreckers, with unclear intentions. A coded Grendel gull message reporting the Corsairs in Madruga was intercepted in Sarvos. Three Wrecker skirmishes were all defeated.

n.Dawn: A great many of the Imperial ships that joined the Corsairs sailed under the flags of Dawn, sharing in the destruction of the Gathered Storm.
n.Grendel: Gallum Firesach's orcs at Mora's Rock defended the Feroz coast from Wreckers and vowed to resist any Confederacy advance, while a Grendel-ciphered message about the Corsairs' presence in Madruga was intercepted before reaching its destination.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: they were the only nation without ships among the Imperial fleets, not being known for maritime prowess.
n.Navarr: Ioan Bloodstride recruited Navarr of Therunin who feel abandoned by the Empire to join a Wrecker raid on Peregro, which was defeated.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn corsairs avenged years of losses by destroying the Gathered Storm and capturing the stolen figurehead, which went to the egregores with hope of reviving the Freeborn Storm, but Suranni forces now hold the Freeborn islands of the Cazar Straits.
n.The League: The Sarvos coast was made safe as the Gathered Storm was destroyed, a Great Chain soldier intercepted a Grendel messenger gull, and Champion of Wisdom Rhydian de Rondell's forces defeated Wreckers at Antonio's Glebe.
n.Urizen: A scattering of Urizeni ships joined the Imperial fleets, and Arbiter of the Four Winds Athenus defeated Wreckers seeking to curse the geysers of Peregro.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark sailors are invoked for the saying that one can never be sure whom an omen favours.

t.Bay of Catazar: With the Gathered Storm destroyed, the Children of Wrecks can no longer directly threaten the Bay's coasts, though some pirate fleets and the corsair Isidore i Boyaga escaped onto its waters.
t.Feroz: The Iron Confederacy crushed the Wreckers in Feroz and conquered the Cazar Straits, while Gallum Firesach's garrison stood ready to defend the coast should the Suranni advance.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the sun is described setting behind its distant mountains.
t.Madruga: The Red Wind Corsairs destroyed the Gathered Storm in Calvos Sound and are now based there, leaving the Wreckers' hold on Madruga tenuous though they still keep Free Landing.
t.Morrow: Wreckers and Navarr recruits attempting to curse Peregro's geysers were defeated by the Arbiter of the Four Winds.
t.Sarvos: The decisive fight began off Trivento, damaged ships sheltered at Caricomare and Trivento, a Grendel gull was shot down, and Wreckers threatening a settlement near Glass Point were defeated at Antonio's Glebe.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Ioan Bloodstride recruited Navarr there who feel the territory has been abandoned by the Empire.
t.Veroigne: Mentioned in passing: one Suranni army was the force Marko Siwarsbairn encountered there earlier in the year.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The Wings of Kobol and two Iron Confederacy armies scoured the Wreckers from the ruins of Shantarim and Cazar, executing captives, and conquered the islands.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni forces made no attempt to approach its coast.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Mentioned in passing: the Suranni did not approach its coast, and Oran is described as still seeking its future.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: The Red Wind Corsairs caught and annihilated the Gathered Storm there, seizing the Storm's Child, and now shelter at Calvos.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The Wreckers failed to reach it before being destroyed but still hold the region, protected by the Maw of Siakha's magical wards.
r.Madruga/Siroc Bayou: Patroco i Boyaga's Wreckers landed in western Siroc Bayou and fled into the Crucible, where Imperial Fleet Master Giovanni von Temeschwar's forces defeated them at Draws Sward.
r.Morrow/Peregro: Wreckers carrying a bottled Spring boon threatened the geysers and the Monastery of the Four Winds' gardens but were defeated at Xavier's Path.

Rose grow the rushes o'.d: After Seeker Alma's Lasambrians killed or captured 200 Strong Reeds, the Reeds rose and freed Graven as three Imperial armies attacked from Mitwold, and Summer heralds and fifteen thousand Lasambrians reinforced the Jotun. Imperial losses were around three thousand and Jotun nearer four thousand. Nearly fifty thousand Jotun with Knights of Glory crossed the Otterway, took Oddmire and Meade, and were halfway through the Meadows when winter snows halted them. Steward's Landing evacuated to Fisk, and Meade's titles lost their resources. Stephen of Sarcombe's attempt to hang Meade's alders sparked fighting with Helma Skutasdóttir. A battle opportunity offered the chance to kill Stephen at Wayford and save the beater Jim Moor.

n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: a thieftaker sought three orc-made swords looted from Imperial orcs killed in the Jotun invasion of Skarsind, now held by Stephen's followers.
n.Jotun: The Jotun lost Graven and most of Gravenmarch to the Empire, but their eight-army invasion took Oddmire, Meade March and Meade. Bjorgthorn Hammerhand's open contempt for Stephen of Sarcombe exposed divisions in their ranks.
n.Navarr: The Bloodcloaks found a cache of healing herbs in Graven, left by Navarr trapped there with a note invoking Liath's Path. No sign of the Navarr remained, and they were presumed executed when Graven fell.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Graven once traded in Brass Coast cerulean mazzarine, and Stephen of Sarcombe's past raids reached Kahraman and Madruga.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Stephen of Sarcombe's past campaign included a strike against the Spider's Dream between Madruga and Sarvos.
n.The Marches: Marcher armies freed Graven and fought side by side in Gravenmarch, while Mitwold suffered its first Jotun invasion in a century or more. Oddmire, Meade March and the city of Meade were lost, and their people were offered the Choice.
n.Wintermark: The Bloodcloaks fought in Gravenmarch, and their healers kept Imperial losses down with the help of the Navarr herb cache. Winterfolk at Fisk took in the evacuated household of Steward's Landing.

t.Bregasland: The Strong Reeds rose and Imperial armies freed Graven, coming four-fifths of the way to reclaiming Gravenmarch against six Jotun armies. Before the rising, Seeker Alma's raid killed or captured 200 Reeds.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the thief Steappa "Nine-Lives" Alpin, who fenced the stolen swords, was a maggot from Hahnmark.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: the eight Jotun armies that invaded Mitwold had rested and provisioned in Liathaven and Hordalant before marching.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: listed among the western territories Stephen of Sarcombe has raided.
t.Kallavesa: Its Wittal Grove borders the Meadows, which raises the threat if the Jotun secure northern Mitwold. Winterfolk across the Gullet at Fisk sheltered the Oddsboy household and pledged to help supply Mitwold's northern shores.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: the eight Jotun armies that invaded Mitwold had rested and provisioned in Liathaven and Hordalant before marching.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Stephen of Sarcombe's past raids included a strike against the Spider's Dream between Madruga and Sarvos.
t.Mitwold: Nearly fifty thousand Jotun conquered Oddmire, Meade March and Meade and reached halfway through the Meadows before winter halted them. Meade's titles lost their resources, and beating the bounds and raiding Kalsea's coast became impossible.
t.Mournwold: Mournwold was sent word of the Mitwold invasion and offered the Imperial armies in Gravenmarch a safe line of retreat through Green March.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: Seeker Alma, the tracker who led the raid on the Strong Reeds, came from the hills of Reinos.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Stephen of Sarcombe's past raids included a strike against the Spider's Dream between Madruga and Sarvos.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: listed among the territories where Stephen of Sarcombe has brought fire and destruction.
t.Skallahn: After Eisa Winterborn fell, her yegarra warband withdrew to its stronghold in Skallahn. It will not return to fight in the Empire until a new champion raises the walrus banner.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the stolen orc swords were looted from Imperial orcs killed during the Jotun invasion of Skarsind years ago.
t.Upwold: The Bounders marched from Upwold to fight in Bregasland, and fear grew that the Jotun might reach their home. The fall of the Meadows would open easy access to Stock March.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: The Strong Reeds and three Imperial armies freed Graven and liberated surrounding villages. The Empire came four-fifths of the way to claiming the region despite Summer heralds and Lasambrian reinforcements.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: At the Autumn Equinox, Imperial heroes intercepted Jotun champions here, bringing down Ghodi Melker and Eisa Winterborn at Leakey Moss.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: A vast Jotun force gathered in Ottermire before crossing the Otterway into Mitwold, and Helma Skutasdóttir planted her banner at Ottery. The Clakes also planned to seize a Jotun supply caravan south of Ottery.
r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: Mentioned in passing: it borders the Meadows, and the Jotun push there could threaten it.
r.Mitwold/Golden Downs: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies in Gravenmarch could circle through Mournwold into the Downs, and Forte Fidelis would struggle if the Jotun turned south-east.
r.Mitwold/Maiden Downs: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies in Gravenmarch could circle through Mournwold into the Downs to return to Mitwold.
r.Mitwold/Meade March: The Jotun overwhelmed Meade's walls, set up a command post in the city and conquered the region. Stephen of Sarcombe's attempt to hang the alders led to bloodshed between Jotun warbands.
r.Mitwold/Oddmire: Oddmire fell within a week and Odd's End opened its gates to avoid destruction. Steward's Landing was abandoned as Jarvey Oddsboy's household fled by boat to Fisk.
r.Mitwold/The Meadows: The Jotun pressed heavily into the Meadows and were halfway to claiming them when worsening winter weather stalled their advance.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Green March remained the Imperial armies' safe line of retreat from Gravenmarch now that the route through Mitwold had been cut.
r.Skallahn/Mindrkyst: Mentioned in passing: Eisa Winterborn's warband withdrew to its stronghold in Skallahn, without naming this region.
r.Upwold/Stock March: Mentioned in passing: Jotun control of the Meadows would give easy access to Stock March.

Rubies in the snow.d: The Narwhal's Spear, Fire of the South, Burning Falcon, Valiant Pegasus, Autumn Hammers and Green Shield gathered at Stark, the Pegasus joined by Summer's Knights of Glory and the Hammers by the Lady of Shikal's siege engines. Greenwall fell almost unopposed. At Kierheim, leaderless since Jarl Ustigar's death, the gates were shattered, but a counter-charge led by Queen Yrsa, who was waiting for a ghodi to settle a three-way succession dispute, threw the Empire back. The Empire was left three-quarters of the way to taking Bjarkey and the northern end of the Kongegőr. The page offered battle opportunities to kill or ransom the ghodi Uksahkka and to turn back Jarl Ebbe's Tromsdalen fyrd, along with three conjunctions.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South came north from Sarangrave, and its general praised the Freeborn for having crushed the Druj.
n.Highguard: The Valiant Pegasus fought in Greenwall and at Kierheim alongside Mistress Malachie's Knights of Glory, sent by Eleonaris in what some magisters suspected was a pointed comment. Highborn soldiers could embrace the knights' urging or turn to their priests for an anointing instead.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Autumn Hammers invoked their contract with the Iron Labyrinth, and the Lady of Shikal's siege engines, towers and great ram broke Kierheim's gates. The orcs still could not hold the city, and the Smith of Ashes was tasked with stopping a Jotun construct from resupplying the garrison.
n.Jotun: The northern Jotun lost Greenwall and most of Bjarkey, and Kierheim held only because Queen Yrsa led the counter-charge in person. With Kierheim's jarldom unresolved and reinforcements not expected before the Solstice, the north risks being split from the southern kingdom.
n.The Marches: Half the Jotun armed force fighting in the Marches owes fealty to Queen Yrsa and may be recalled to defend Skallahn. The Bailiff of Meade was tasked with rescuing the shipwrecked Marcher raiders of the Old Jim's Ewe on Drekatangi beach.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark hosted the gathering at Stark, and its Narwhal's Spear and Green Shield were at the forefront of the assault. Iron Osric had killed Jarl Ustigar, and the Strategos of Wintermark was charged with killing Jarl Eluf and recovering a Kallavesi Spiritskin Coat.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Queen Yrsa's army is engaged in Bregasland, and messengers are racing there to recall the northern jarls.
t.Bryadvik: Mentioned in passing: a rumoured fast ship sailed to Bryadvik to summon its jarls, who are expected to answer the Queen's call.
t.Fjorknae: Mentioned in passing: rumours say a ship went to call Fjorknae's jarls to Skallahn, and it was where Ustigar and Ebbe once hunted monsters in their youth.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: the Kongegőr bridge links Skallahn to Hordalant, and messengers are passing through it heading south.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: most of the southern armies marched north through Kallavesa, and the Kallavesi Braerhal lost their thane and a Spiritskin Coat in Greenwall.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: the Autumn Hammers had been billeted here before marching north, and Jotun messengers are heading here to recall the jarls.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Burning Falcon marched north from Mournwold to join the invasion.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South travelled from Sarangrave, the longest journey of any army.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: a rumoured Jotun ship braved the winter gales into the Sea of Snow to summon the western jarls.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq was the staging ground for the invasion, with six Imperial armies camped around the Fortress of Kalant in Stark before marching west.
t.Skallahn: The Empire seized Greenwall and three-quarters of Bjarkey, and Kierheim's walls and garrison were badly damaged though the city held. A succession crisis kept the Queen there while fyrds and reinforcements gathered.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Unshackled were used to the cold from Skarsind's snowy mountains.
t.Tromsa: Tromsa's jarls are expected to send reinforcements, and Jarl Ebbe the Snowboar marches south with the Tromsdalen fyrd. The ghodi Uksahkka travels with the forces moving from Tromsa.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the Green Shield marched north from Upwold to join the invasion.

r.Sermersuaq/Stark: The six Imperial armies gathered here in a sea of tents around the Fortress of Kalant, enduring hail and snow before the invasion began.
r.Skallahn/Bjarkey: The Empire overran most of Bjarkey and broke Kierheim's gates but was driven back, leaving it three-quarters conquered. Taking it would give the Empire the northern end of the Kongegőr.
r.Skallahn/Greenwall: Greenwall fell entirely to the Empire, leaving its thralls bewildered by their liberation. Jarl Eluf Asbjørnsson retreated and raised the region's fyrd.
r.Skallahn/Iron Stand: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Eluf's hall lies near Greenwall's northern border with Iron Stand.
r.Skallahn/Ulfrsmoor: Mentioned in passing: warriors from the fort of Ulfrsborg reinforced the defence of Greenwall and Kierheim.
r.Tromsa/Majastind: Queen Yrsa sent to Mount Majastind for a ghodi who hears Ulven's voice clearly, to choose Kierheim's new jarl.
r.Tromsa/Tromsdalen: Jarl Ebbe raised the Tromsdalen fyrd of nearly a thousand to honour his oaths to Ustigar, and it would return home if he fell. The ghodi Uksahkka also travels south from Mount Tromsdalen.

Scarlet sands.d: Four Broken Shore armies had pushed north from Ayereed. The Naguerro besieged the newly finished Grand Lodge and demanded seasonal 'rent', while the Iron Gulls, Storm Sharks and Brine Turtles assailed the Fundindelve. General Ansleah's demands alienated Clisearn's former Grendel families. The Imperial armies, aided by magical allies, drove the Grendel back to Fioroult, losing nearly two thousand soldiers against comparable enemy losses. The Empire is three-tenths of the way to securing Fleisardh. The Lodge and Ruicraic's Redoubt removed the Uncooperative quality from Clisearn and Eoradal, and Beoraidh stayed neutral. The opportunity offers stopping a cliff-collapsing Winter boon, breaking a seal to poison the Brine Turtles' lake, extracting a reaver, and killing questioner Kester.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun had just been fighting the Druj in the Sarangrave before marching south to Mareave.
n.Grendel: The Broken Shore armies were driven out of Clisearn and back to Fioroult in Fleisardh at heavy cost. General Ansleah's heavy-handed demands also pushed Clisearn's former Grendel families further from Attar.
n.Highguard: The Seventh Wave marched along Carstag's Way to join the campaign, helped retake Clisearn and drove the Brine Turtles from the Tholdie estates.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Winter Sun led the counter-attack to defend Mareave's settlers. Imperial success, with a warband of Uthni youths joining them, began to win over the territory's independent orcs.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Naguerro's cousins in Hierro and Corazón are said to have rebuilt their pride with the aid of the Jotun.
n.The League: The Towerjacks marched through Spiral to fight in Clisearn and secure the Golden Pyramid Lodge, and some were invited to inspect the near-complete Ruicraic's Redoubt.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun marched through Zenith and the armies passed through sodden Proceris on their way south.

t.Ayereed: The Grendel land forces launched their invasion north from Ayereed, and the Empire hopes to drive them back there.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Naguerro once sailed the western Bay, and Fleisardh's cliffs, threatened by a Grendel boon, face the Bay.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks' general recalled the Imperial Orcs rallying to lift the siege of Holberg.
t.Mareave: The Empire drove the Grendel out of Clisearn and advanced into Fleisardh. Imperial successes and the completion of the Grand Lodge and Ruicraic's Redoubt eased the hostility of the independent orcs.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: only the name connects it, through Ruicraic's Redoubt, a fortification being completed in Eoradal in Mareave.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun came south from fighting slavery and the Druj in the Sarangrave.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the Naguerro were once fierce sailors and a thorn in the side of the people of Sarvos.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the chill of the Winter fortress in Nadir relieved Imperial Orcs used to Skarsind's alpine climate.
t.Spiral: The Winter Sun and Towerjacks crossed Spiral as quickly as they could, pausing at Ballaghadruh. The oppressive power of the Black Plateau took a toll in night terrors and dark moods.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun marched south into Zenith to join the Towerjacks before heading for Mareave.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Beoraidh stayed neutral under the patronage of the Sarcophan Delves, welcoming both Imperial and Grendel merchants, which kept the Grendel from threatening the northern regions.
r.Mareave/Clisearn: The Naguerro besieged the Golden Pyramid Grand Lodge and the other armies assailed the Fundindelve until Imperial armies drove them out. The Lodge's completion removed the region's Uncooperative quality.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: The Imperial armies mustered at the Basalt Citadel conjured by the Lord Sorin. Uthni youths joined the Winter Sun, and the completed Ruicraic's Redoubt removed the Uncooperative quality.
r.Mareave/Fleisardh: The Grendel fell back to Fioroult and the Empire is three-tenths of the way to securing the region, which remains Uncooperative and Under Threat. The Capstone Veld battle opportunity is set here, including a Winter boon threatening the cliffs and a seal protecting the Brine Turtles' lake.
r.Mareave/Icarion: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial armies marched through Icarion's arid hills from the Apulian Way to Eoradal.
r.Mareave/Nadir: Six basalt towers from the Queen of Ice and Darkness's demesne appeared in Nadir's foothills, and a legion of white-bear warriors joined the armies passing through.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: Mentioned in passing: the armies moved as swiftly as possible through Apstrus towards the Apulian Way.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Mentioned in passing: the armies carried mud from their passage through sodden Proceris, which soon turned to dust in Mareave.

Search high and low.d: The Mournwold Breadbasket would need Senate approval and cost 15 white granite, 35 weirwood and 150 crowns over two seasons. It would give every Mournwold farm 36 extra rings a season and let the Marches support one more army once Bregasland is regained. Stockwater Monastery offered up to ten wains of white granite at 18 mana per wain. Anne Craig's Wayford alders offered ten weirwood for 28 thrones. Harry the Axe offered five weirwood if the Assembly declared with a greater majority that Alderly belongs to the Feni. A Keeper's Cottage could be built in the Mournwold, Upwold or Mitwold. Building both would open further opportunities.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun hold Bregasland, and Marchers are confident they will be driven out, as they were from the Mournwold.
n.The Marches: Marchers were urged to answer the Assembly's highest calling by completing the Breadbasket, which would enrich Mournwold farms and let the nation support an extra army once Bregasland is retaken. Several Marchers offered materials, though Harry's price of recognising the Feni claim to Alderly stirred contempt.

t.Bregasland: Under Jotun occupation, Bregasland was ruled out as a site for the Keeper's Cottage, and the Breadbasket's extra army support depends on the Marches retaking it.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: many of the Alderly Feni who fled the Marcher attack are said to have ended up in Liathaven.
t.Mitwold: The Wayford alders wanted the Keeper's Cottage built in Mitwold, where it would give the Keeper 12 crowns a season, and offered ten weirwood for 28 thrones.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold was the proposed site of the final Breadbasket great work, which would add 36 rings a season to every farm there. A Keeper's Cottage there would yield 12 random ingots a season.
t.Upwold: Stockwater Monastery in Upwold offered its stored white granite, saved to rebuild its crumbling transept, in exchange for mana. It also offered land for the Keeper's Cottage, which would yield 12 liao a season there.

r.Mournwold/Alderly: Woodcutter Harry the Axe offered five wains of Alderly weirwood if the Marcher Assembly declared with a greater majority that Alderly Woods belongs to the Feni, some of whom reportedly still live deeper in the woods.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Mentioned in passing: metals from the Ore Hills mines would supply the ingot income of a Keeper's Cottage built in the Mournwold.

Shadow in the grass.d: Imperial heroes destroyed all four Falconer pillars and slew three of its four Voices. Only the Voice of the Fount survived, fleeing powerless into the wastes, while scattered cultists remain. Big Icebarn was supported by over 24,000 strength, but fewer than 7,000 came from Wintermark, and it was forced back into Sydanjaa. It still drew out the Ceaseless Hunter and the Feasting Lord. Conjunctions to slay them fall to Ceolmund Dreth and Maryc of House Orzel. The Hunt the Suaq Wastes venture now yields rings, Wasteland vis and, for strong units, interdicted Keen Lifeblood. Eawyn Icerunner's crossing of Nutjuitoq opened options to scout or appraise Tsirku.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the page notes there are no Jotun armies in Sermersuaq and that the Suaq Wastes' monsters have plagued the land since it was lost to the Jotun in 382YE.
n.Thule: Thule forces killed the Voice of the Peaks and dealt with the Falconer pillar in the north-east mountains, playing their part in the cult's defeat.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's heroes and their allies emphatically defeated the Cult of the Falconer. However, the nation's small share of support for Big Icebarn saw the artok driven back north, and its Banner-bearer of Atkonaroq, Ceolmund Dreth, must now lead heroes to slay the Ceaseless Hunter.

t.Sermersuaq: The territory has been largely freed from the Falconer cult and the Winter monsters, though cultist remnants and more aggressive beasts still trouble remote halls, held in check by the garrisons of Olgafsdottirshal and the Fortress of Kalant.
t.Tsirku: Tsirku, a storm-wracked wasteland beyond the inland sea of Nutjuitoq, could now host an Imperial spy network or be appraised for exploitation. Neither option would reveal anything about Sydanjaa.

r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Two conjunctions offer the chance to kill Agramant's last great guardians in the Wastes, the Ceaseless Hunter and the Feasting Lord. The Hunt the Suaq Wastes venture now rewards units with rings, Wasteland vis and, for the strongest, Keen Lifeblood.

The circle game.d: Graciana concluded that most citizens and foreigners prefer coin to barter. Following Emperor Giovanni's design, money spent at Anvil circulates back to the treasury, and it is lost only through armies, fortifications and ministries. She offered several options: abrogating the Grandmaster mana ministries, which would put an extra 127 crystal mana a season into the font; ending embassy ministries; and converting the Northern trade network into great works. She advised against touching the six Prosperity ministries. She found barter deals with Axos, the Sarcophan Kruidenkenner and the Ossium Ketsov. She also reviewed outstanding great works in Feroz, Sermersuaq, Kallavesa, Madruga, Karov and Zenith. Finally, she suggested Synod mandates urging League and Marcher citizens to take up businesses and farms.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Boar's Market is one of the Prosperity ministries Graciana advised against abrogating. If the Kallavesa Marshways were built, Dawnish military units would gain a guarding venture protecting merchants there.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page and is linked only through its share of Feroz, where the Inkworks of Joharra opportunity remains open.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Cinder Path Exchange, the first of the Prosperity ministries, should be left alone according to Graciana. Separately, the House of Spirits in Casinea could trade liao to the Axou for ilium if the Senate accepted their offer.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Torfast Trading Post in Skarsind anchors the Northern trade network. Graciana proposed upgrading it to a great work that would trade the Bonesetter's routes for higher business investment across the territory.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland, now held by the Jotun, is noted as no longer under Imperial control, which rules out building the Marshways there.
n.Navarr: Navarr's Invisible Cord Brokerage is a Prosperity ministry Graciana advised keeping. The Treji Wayhouse in Hercynia could be converted into a great work boosting herb gardens. Therunin's lost status means no Marshways can be built there.
n.The Brass Coast: The Parador of Dust is a protected Prosperity ministry, and two Freeborn opportunities remain open. The Inkworks of Joharra in Feroz would create a Scrivener of the Inkworks title. The Municipal Docks in Madruga would raise taxation, fleets and businesses and add a Quaymaster title.
n.The League: Graciana proposed a Synod mandate urging League citizens to invest in businesses, letting them convert other resources for free and upgrade businesses for one wain less for a year. Temeschwar's Northbound Trademaster could also become a great work once the rest of the network is upgraded.
n.Thule: The Thule take part in the Northern trade network, exchanging crystal mana for Imperial ingots and measures. Their Urdur trade is the only option each ministry would keep if converted into a great work.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Graciana notes a new appraisal by Naomi of Virtue's Rest proposing roads in Zenith to raise business investment there.
n.Varushka: The Iron Tower is a protected Prosperity ministry. The Ketsov of Ossium would accept ingots instead of coin for herbs, and Delev in Karov could receive either a modest market conversion or the larger Great Market, but not both.
n.Wintermark: The motion came from Sermersuaq's senator, and Wintermark scholar Vauraus Korppitkotka's analysis was confirmed by the appraisal. Several Wintermark opportunities are listed: the Kauppahall is protected, the Kalpaheim Tradehall, Atalaq Fishery and Tradehall, and Kallavesa Marshways remain open, and the Marshways would add a guarding venture for Wintermark units.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland was part of the original Marshways plan but is no longer controlled by the Empire, so building there is out of the question.
t.Casinea: The Bursar of the House of Spirits in Casinea could acquire ilium from the Axou in exchange for large amounts of liao, if the Senate accepted the offer.
t.Feroz: The Inkworks of Joharra remains available for 60 white granite and 60 crowns. It would raise business investment in Feroz, boost scriveners' income for a year and create the Scrivener of the Inkworks.
t.Hahnmark: The Kalpaheim Tradeholder's ministry could be converted into the Kalpaheim Tradehall great work. This would raise business investment across Hahnmark by one while leaving the title only the Urdur trade.
t.Hercynia: The Treji Wayhouse could become a great work that raises herb garden investment in Hercynia by one, removing the Broker's other trade options apart from the Urdur trade.
t.Kallavesa: Updated Marshways plans for Kallavesa alone would cost 80 wains of weirwood and 240 crowns. They would raise investment in businesses and herb gardens and create a guarding venture for Wintermark and Dawnish units.
t.Karov: Delev could see either the Delev Market great work, which requires the other northern upgrades first, or Naomi's larger Great Market at Delev. The Great Market would add four thrones of taxation but would increase spending by several ministries.
t.Madruga: The Municipal Docks proposal for Calvos remains open. It would raise investment in fleets and businesses, add 12 thrones of taxation for 5 thrones of upkeep, and give Freeborn characters extra income for a year.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: the opening fiction recalls Giovanni's Miaren campaign as a moment of heroism that he apparently regarded as a disaster.
t.Ossium: The Ketsov would accept ingots instead of coin for the herbs bought by the Merchant-Boyar of the Stinking Market and the Apothecary of Orieb. Graciana warned this would make both ministries depend on the often touchy Ketsov.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the Sarvos mana exchange was among those expanded in 384YE to enhance the Grandmasters' ministries, and economist Laurencio Lemmini di Sarvos is cited.
t.Sermersuaq: The appraisal was raised by Sermersuaq's senator. Two opportunities remain open there: the Atalaq Fishery, which would raise farm investment, and the Atalaq Tradehall, which would raise business investment and add 4 thrones of taxation.
t.Skarsind: The Torfast Trading Post, anchor of the Northern trade network, could become a great work raising business investment across Skarsind. The Bonesetter would be left with only the northern Urdur route.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is noted as the seat of the Imperial Mint established by Giovanni and as one of the expanded mana exchanges.
t.Temeschwar: The Northbound Trademaster's ministry could be converted into the Northbound Trade great work, raising business investment, but only once every other branch of the northern network is upgraded. It would work well alongside the Silver Fox Mines.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Therunin was in the original Marshways plan but is suffering invasion and is no longer Imperial, so it was dropped.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Naomi of Virtue's Rest has proposed roads in Zenith that would raise business investment in the territory.

r.Feroz/Oranseri: The Inkworks of Joharra would be built in Oranseri, and its completion would remove the region's impoverished quality.
r.Hahnmark/Kalpamark: Kalpamark is the site of the proposed Kalpaheim Tradehall great work, costing 30 wains of white granite, 90 crowns and three months.
r.Hercynia/The Glen of Shadows: The Treji Wayhouse in the Glen of Shadows could be upgraded into a great work for 30 wains of white granite and 90 crowns to boost Hercynian herb gardens.
r.Karov/Duzekani: Delev in Duzekani is the site of two mutually exclusive proposals: the Delev Market great work or the larger Great Market at Delev.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: The Municipal Docks would be built at Calvos. They would protect Calvos Sound as a level one fortification and serve as a shipyard for up to two navies.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Mentioned in passing: completing the Municipal Docks would create a new Freeborn questing voyage, Hunt the Free Landing Kraken.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: Sealtoq would host both the Atalaq Fishery and the Atalaq Tradehall, centred on the town of Atalaq.
r.Skarsind/Southpine: The Torfast Trading Post in Southpine could be upgraded to a great work for 30 wains of white granite, 90 crowns and three months.
r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: Hanuri is the site of the proposed Northbound Trade great work, costing 60 wains of white granite and 180 crowns. It depends on the rest of the northern network being upgraded first.

The concisest tenant.d: Rumours of an ancient rat spirit beneath Temeschwar persist, and plays of the Steadfast Soldier and the King of Rats are thriving. Temeschwari citizens wearing a Doctor's mask could draw on cold resolve, and League magicians could channel the Doctor in Day or Winter rituals. The Rat Kings planned to attend the Masquerade of the Reaper at Anvil. With Giselle reinterred in Sarvos, Bishop Jarek proposed recasting Virtue's Respite as a monument to Temeschwari Pride, with a Pride of the City lecture. Lorainne Brouat proposed a Rat Garden acknowledging the rat spirit, which the Unfettered Mind wished to study. Either option needs a Senate motion and would allow the Guardian's title to be renamed.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: their sacking of Sarvos and theft of Giselle's body are recalled as the origin of the memorial, and the rebuilding of Sarvos after their attack appears on its friezes.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the escort of Giselle's body from Highguard to Temeschwar is depicted on one of Virtue's Respite's friezes.
n.The League: League citizens in Temeschwar could draw on the Doctor's influence, and League magicians could channel it in ritual. The League Assembly could also spread a Pride of the City lecture to every League city, though this risked stoking fierce rivalry over which city is greatest.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar was once Varushkan land, the King of Rats tale has Varushkan origins, and the rat spirit is likened to what Varushkans call a sovereign.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the liberation of Holberg appears on the friezes of Virtue's Respite, and Holberg is said to have recently claimed the crown of greatest League city.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the bravo Lorainne Brouat fought alongside Varushkan armies in the conquest of Ossium.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Empress Giselle's remains now rest in a courtyard at Capodomus Cathedral in Sarvos, leaving her Temeschwar tomb empty.
t.Temeschwar: The city's rats now mostly come out at night thanks to the Rat Kings, while the rat-masked Doctor lent its citizens and magicians cold strength. The city faced a choice over remodelling Virtue's Respite as either a shrine to Temeschwari Pride or a Rat Garden acknowledging the spirit beneath its streets.

r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: Virtue's Respite stands in Hanuri, and both proposed commissions to remodel it as a Pride memorial or a Rat Garden would be carried out there, raising the Guardian's income.
r.Temeschwar/Metri: Mentioned in passing: the victory over the night terrors of Metri is suggested as a subject for new Temeschwari friezes at Virtue's Respite.

The price is great.d: The Diplomatenschloss in Necropolis was finished and garrisoned by veteran Commonwealth soldiers under Commander Inka Kraul, who echoed concerns about Jarmish vessels on the Couros. Three possible commissions for a river patrol were outlined: a Highborn Coursguard at Haros Water, an Urizen River Sentinel at Couros Seat, or a joint River Watcher. Militärattache Schöningen dismissed fears about Commonwealth diplomats aiding Asavea. She warned that the Surveyors' Cartel alleged Imperial trade with Jarm through Zemelslo. The Sternemetal Tower and mana-for-goods trade were withdrawn. Leerdam philosophers might visit Dawn if its National Assembly passed a suitable statement. The University of Volkavaar took the sungold tablet and offered help restoring Therunin.

n.Dawn: Lord Sable's interest in discussing love led Leerdam's Hochschule der Seele to offer a visit. If the National Assembly backed a statement welcoming Commonwealth guests with a greater majority, Dawnish congregations could host lectures on The Universality of Love, receive gifts and join the Assembly of the Way.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the University of Volkavaar offered help restoring Therunin once it is liberated from the Druj.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel's past attacks on the mouth of the Couros and its bridges were cited as a reason to secure the river.
n.Highguard: Highguard gained a garrisoned Commonwealth embassy in Necropolis and might create a Coursguard title at Haros Water to keep peace on the Couros. Its Prognosticator's Office could also be sent to the Commonwealth to carry out an appraisal.
n.Navarr: A Navarr broker proposed the compromise of joint patrol quays in Reikos and Morrow. The Couros also forms part of the border with the vallorn of Therunin.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: an earlier invitation for Commonwealth citizens to visit Holberg was cited, as were the unfulfilled assurances of the previous ambassador Lucia Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Commander Kraul privately likened the Empire's view of Jarm to its view of Jarm's Thule neighbours.
n.Urizen: The architects of Cargo argued that the river patrol should be Urizen, which opened the option of a River Sentinel at Couros Seat in Morrow or a joint title with Highguard. Concern also centred on the Jarmish embassy in Cargo.
n.Wintermark: The Imperial ambassador, Finn Pridetalker of Wintermark, had his concerns about Asavea dismissed and his crystal mana offer declined. He was given warning of Commonwealth accusations of Imperial trade with Jarm so that he could prepare a response.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the Couros was described as a border between the Highborn heartlands and other lands.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: last year's invitation for Commonwealth citizens to visit Holberg was cited as a precedent for the Dawnish visit.
t.Morrow: The spire of Couros Seat in Morrow was proposed as an alternative site for a river patrol commission, or as one half of a joint Highborn-Urizen one.
t.Necropolis: The Commonwealth Diplomatenschloss was completed in Necropolis. A veteran Commonwealth garrison under Inka Kraul took up residence to protect the embassy and the territory, and Kraul toured the territory, admiring Reumah's Rest.
t.Redoubt: The Jarmish embassy in Cargo worried Commonwealth officers, and Cargo's architects argued that the river watch should be based on the Urizen side rather than at Haros Water.
t.Reikos: Haros Water in Reikos was proposed as the site of the Haros Riverpatrol, a sinecure creating the Highborn Coursguard to keep peace on the Couros and Haros rivers.
t.Therunin: The University of Volkavaar offered to help appraise how Therunin might be restored once it is liberated from the Druj, and took the sungold tablet recovered from its northern sinkhole.

r.Morrow/Ravion: Couros Seat in eastern Ravion was put forward as a site for an Urizen River Sentinel or as part of the joint Couros Patrol Quays.
r.Reikos/Haros Water: Haros Water was proposed for the Haros Riverpatrol or the joint Couros Patrol Quays, which would guard against pirates, raiders and clashes between Jarm and the Commonwealth.
r.Reikos/Riverwatch: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, though the proposed river patrol is referred to as a riverwatch.

The thing with feathers.d: Agramant's heralds began aiding starving Navarr in Therunin and offered boons for Unleash the Beasts Within and Treacher's Quill. Sorin sent the Sepulchral Pontifex to the Imperial Orcs to honour a year of Basalt Citadels at Eoradal. Irra Harah offered the Gryphon's Pride the chance to finish watchtowers in Nesustak Forest, and Llofir asked the Vallornguard to ease the dying in Eastring. Janon sent a ring for the next Shadowed Torchbearer, and the Whisper Gallery turned its attacks on the Magpies, with a skirmish foreseen in Hahnmark. Knights of Glory continued to bind armies, prompting a possible Highborn mandate. Cathan Canae's test at Hope's Rest needed one final casting, and Estavus finalised an office at Iteri.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Phoenix Rising coven needed one more Frozen Citadel at Hope's Rest to complete Cathan Canae's test. Separately, Irra Harah invited the Gryphon's Pride under Ser Guy of the Twisted Rose to help the Sarangrave rebels build watchtowers.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj appear as the foe behind the Knights of Glory reliance and the Hope's Rest citadel offer, and Agramant would hand out potions taken from Druj remnants in Therunin.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Callidus's herald Multitudo asked the Imperial Ambassador to the Grendel, Starlight Starchaser, to join a private discussion of "sashes and shields".
n.Highguard: Following Frater Pontius's upheld judgement, the Highborn Assembly could enact a mandate for its soldiers to shun heralds. This would restore cautious advance and give ground orders to its armies, but at a cost of 1000 strength when supported by heralds.
n.Imperial Orcs: Sorin's Sepulchral Pontifex came to the Imperial Orc camp to honour the Heralds of the Reaper's year of Basalt Citadels at Eoradal and to weigh an undisclosed offer. Heralds of Ylenwe sought Archmage Skywise Gralka as a guide to dance, and heralds of Janon came to watch the orc fighting pit.
n.Navarr: Navarr cut off in Therunin were increasingly accepting Agramant's aid, and the Howler offered extra strength and Druj potions to Navarr units enchanted with Unleash the Beasts Within. Llofir also asked the Vallornguard to grant peaceful deaths to those suffering in Eastring.
n.Urizen: Estavus finalised plans for an Office of Fire and Stone in Zenith with a new Architect of Hammers title. Agramant offered Urizen magicians foci or a relic for performing Treacher's Quill on Therunin, and Bartimaeus was named a "Prince" of Callidus's auction.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka's territory Ossium was named among the conquests discussed when the now-broken Fist of the Black Glacier ritual was first awarded.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Vanja Oddsbreaker, the first Shadowed Torchbearer, had vacated her post, prompting Janon to send a ring for her successor. A Whisper Gallery attack on the Magpies near Gulnar's Depths in Hahnmark was foreseen as a skirmish for the following summit.

t.Hahnmark: Servants of the Whisper Gallery attacked Magpies near Gulnar's Depths, where Vanya Heartsworn may have found a clue to the lost hammer Avalanche. A skirmish there was foreseen for the Spring Equinox.
t.Mareave: The Heralds of the Reaper's year-long defence of Mareave with the Basalt Citadel won the grudging respect of Sorin's Monarch of the Silent Kingdom.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium was one of the conquests whose strategy generals once discussed with a castellan of Cathan Canae.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Mourningstone Navarr escaped from Therunin across the border into Chalcis Mount in Reikos to bring their warning.
t.Sarangrave: The Sarangrave rebels sought the Gryphon's Pride's help to build watchtowers in Nesustak Forest. The lasting effects of Knights of Glory on armies were observed most clearly here.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq was named among the conquests discussed when the Fist of the Black Glacier ritual was awarded.
t.The Barrens: A final Frozen Citadel at Hope's Rest would complete Cathan Canae's test, bringing a permanent wintry quality and a strong citadel offer to the southern Barrens.
t.Therunin: Agramant's heralds were active in Therunin, buying the loyalty of desperate Navarr with aid. Llofir also sought peaceful deaths for those suffering after fighting vallornspawn in Eastring.
t.Zenith: The Architects of Iron and Stone finalised an Office of Fire and Stone at the Crucible of Fate in Zenith, available to commission until the end of Autumn 388YE.

r.Mareave/Eoradal: The ruins of Eoradal had hosted Sorin's Basalt Citadel every season for a year, earning the Silent Kingdom's notice.
r.Reikos/Chalcis Mount: Mentioned in passing: a haggard group of Navarr crossed out of Therunin into Chalcis Mount to warn of Agramant's activities.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: If the Gryphon's Pride gave a supporting defensive order, rebel watchtowers would be finished by Spring 388YE, removing the region's under-threat status.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: One more Frozen Citadel would make Hope's Rest Rimebound, empowering Summer enchantments there. It would also offer Dawn a permanent Citadel of the Rimebound Shore for 100 rings of ilium.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: Mentioned in passing: the Last Battle Wayhouse in the Bleaks was the source of the threat hanging over Nesustak Forest.
r.Therunin/Eastring: Llofir asked the Speaker of the Vallornguard to travel with the vines to Eastring and give painless deaths to those who could not be saved, near a strangely behaving vallornspawn briar.
r.Zenith/Iteri: The proposed Office of Fire and Stone would stand at the Crucible of Fate in Iteri. It would let heralds of Estavus enter there regardless of alignment.

The truth but tell it slant.d: Impressed by Tassato's use of movable type, Gelberg proposed three options. The first was a Printers' Guild Grand Guildhouse in Tassato Mestra, raising the Guild's Museum and Mausoleum incomes, allowing a publication to be spread each season, and granting one address to the Empire. The second was a Bibliopole offering translated publications in Betovering and Leerdam. The third was a Publishing Clearing House great work, adding 36 rings to every Tassato business and boosting the Printmaster of Cevia. Carina Schiver added an edifice to renovate Moor's Mill in Tassato Regario, promoting ringblack novels. If the Chair of the Wolf commissioned any of these, extra benefits would follow. All remain proposals.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is named as a place where interest in ringblack novels would grow if Moor's Mill were supported.
n.The League: The League's printers, guilds and Chair of the Wolf were offered several commissions that could make Tassato the printing centre of the Empire, or even the world. One option would also foster a new literary movement of ringblack novels celebrating League vigilance.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: travellers from Thule's Otkodov might take an interest in the proposed Publishing Clearing House.

t.Bastion: If the Chair of the Wolf completed the Moor's Mill investment, Esmeralda di Rodez offered to donate a relic of Berechiah to the title running Berechiah's Basilica in Bastion. This would follow once both relevant commissions were complete.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Chair of the Wolf, the title able to gain extra benefits from these commissions, was established in Holberg with the support of its College of Engineering.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: travellers from Otkodov are named as potential visitors drawn by the Publishing Clearing House.
t.Tassato: Tassato stood to gain a grand guildhouse, a Publishing Clearing House adding 36 rings to every business in the territory, and a renovated Moor's Mill press. Together these would cement the city as the Empire's centre of printing.

r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: Tassato Mestra, home to the Printers' Guild enclave, was the proposed site of both the Grand Guildhouse and the riverside Publishing Clearing House.
r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: Tassato Regario's Moor's Mill printworks, revived by youths printing "Stories of the Vigilant", could be renovated as an edifice. If consecrated by the Vigilance assembly, it might inspire League vigilance.

The tune without the words.d: Agents of the Moonsilver King prompted the addition of Bells of Silver and Brass and Might of Vstaive to Urizen lore. A gift for Ibiss Briarheart added three illegal Siakha rituals. The Children of Wrecks' Thunderous Deluge battered Madruga, Feroz and Sarvos, where flood defences saved the city but Riposi's cliffs collapsed. Night magic in Madruga stirred rebellious sentiment, empowered a transformative pool and offered marsh flowers. Strange dreams touched the Gullet territories, and coral husks took the dead into the sea. Conjunctions were raised in Hercynia and Therunin. The Crimson Reapers announced an auction of the Loom of Spells, the last faux constellations vanished from memory, and the Silent Market reopened.

n.Dawn: The Roses of Racqueen, a Weaver cabal from Semmerholm, contributed Might of Vstaive to Urizen lore. Strangers sought tales of fear in Astolat and Weirwater, and Dawnish folk in the Barrens heard the Navarri song in their dreams.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as destroyers of the Halls of Knowledge and as overrunning Therunin, driving out the Glimmerwater steading.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel are not named; their link is through Feroz, which the cursed storms struck heavily.
n.Highguard: Strangers asking for stories of fear were reported on the roads to Casinea, and unfamiliar faux constellations had earlier appeared over Necropolis.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is listed among the territories where faux constellations appeared after the Spring Equinox.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are noted as claiming Bregasland and pressing the Fenlanders, and the Green Shield's attack into Skallahn is referred to.
n.Navarr: Nathair Autumngale's arcane projection spread dreams of the song Painted to every Navarr, offering pride in their oaths. Navarri also face a disturbing conjunction in Hercynia, and the Glimmerwater steading has fled Therunin with its merrow lantern.
n.The Brass Coast: Cursed storms battered Madruga and Feroz, while Night magic in Madruga stirred a rebellious love of liberty against Azir i Shartha i Riqueza's statement on Anarchy. It also strengthened naga and briar trappings at a Crucible pool and opened a chance to grow marsh flowers.
n.The League: Sarvos weathered the Thunderous Deluge thanks to Senator Rosalina Gulia Viola di Sarvos's flood defences, though Riposi was ravaged. Spiral remains steeped in dramaturgical magic, and the Crimson Reapers will auction use of the Loom of Spells.
n.The Marches: Mitwold folk shared strange dreams tied to the Gullet. Bill of Middleton, Keeper of the Dour Fens, must lead a group against coral husks in North Fens.
n.Urizen: Five new rituals entered Urizen lore: two that restore and strengthen garrisons, and three illegal Siakha rituals. Urizeni in Spiral continue to experience its theatrical strangeness.
n.Varushka: Strangers asking for tales of fear were encountered across all five Varushkan territories. Faux constellations had earlier hung over Karov.
n.Wintermark: Kallavesa saw strange Gullet dreams, and coral husks massed in West Marsh and Stark, to be dealt with by the Watcher of Britta's Pool and the Academy. The Silent Market made an offer to Wintermark casters for provably Hahnmark viezesmaak.

t.Astolat: Travellers reported strangers on the roads asking for stories of fear and paying a token ingot or two in thanks.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Bastion is not named; it falls only within the general account of the vanished penumbral veils and faux constellations.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar is not named; the page touches on related sea-storm magic of Siakha and her Children of Wrecks.
t.Bregasland: Sensitive folk had vivid dreams linked to the Gullet, and coral husks massed in North Fens to drag away the dead.
t.Brocéliande: Nathair Autumngale led hundreds of Navarr through the Sentinel Gate to a Night regio here to cast An Ode To Blood And Sacrifice. The song dreams spread outward from here along the trods.
t.Casinea: Strangers asking for tales of fear were met on the roads to Casinea. The territory was one of the few untouched by the penumbral veils.
t.Feroz: The Thunderous Deluge hit rebuilding Feroz hard, flooding the Scorrero and soaking makeshift homes. Wisps of Madruga's Night enchantment spilled over, letting herb gardens be diversified to grow marsh flowers.
t.Hahnmark: The Silent Market offered Wintermark casters narcotics or Imperial Roseweald or Cerulean Mazzarine in exchange for viezesmaak sworn to come from Hahnmark's farms. Faux constellations had earlier hung overhead.
t.Hercynia: An injured Navarri reported troubling events at the remote Starwood Roots Steading. The Archmage of Winter is charged with investigating a conjunction there involving gore and hints of cannibalism.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg is listed among the territories where faux constellations appeared around the Summer Solstice.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa was one of the centres of the strange Gullet dreams, and coral husks are hunting for corpses in West Marsh.
t.Karov: Strangers seeking stories of fear walked Karov's roads as in the rest of Varushka, and faux constellations had earlier appeared above it.
t.Madruga: Madruga was soaked by cursed storms and wrapped in Night magic that brought transformative dreams, active heralds of Azoth and Janon, and a fierce urge for liberty. It also opened chances to grow marsh flowers and seek hallows of Anarchy.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold was one of the main territories where folk dreamed of floods, drowned seas and a terrible living thing in warm waters.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is not named; it falls only within the general account of the vanished penumbral veils and faux constellations.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold is listed as untouched by the penumbral veils, yet also among the places where faux constellations appeared after the Spring Equinox.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis is listed among the territories where faux constellations appeared after the Spring Equinox.
t.Redoubt: The Shield of Thought coven of Willstone Citadel contributed Bells of Silver and Brass to Urizen lore. Redoubt's lightstone is mentioned in the opening tale.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: Sarangrave is excluded from the lingering urge to recall the vanished faux constellations.
t.Sarvos: Wreckers used the Circle of Savagery to curse Sarvos with months of storms. Flood defences built with the Vandersaar family protected the City of Masks, though Rodez, Trivento and Riposi suffered.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: the Sea of Snow is not named; the page's sea-related events concern the Gullet and other waters.
t.Semmerholm: The Roses of Racqueen, a Weaver cabal from Semmerholm, gave Might of Vstaive to Urizen lore in return for undisclosed boons. Faux constellations had earlier hung over the territory.
t.Sermersuaq: Jimothy o' Hay spotted coral husks in Stark, and the Academy's students are to investigate.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: the Green Shield's attack into Skallahn is referred to in passing.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is listed among the territories where faux constellations appeared after the Spring Equinox.
t.Spiral: Spiral's theatrical magical convocation has grown stronger, filling the city with drama. Resident League and Urizen citizens can draw on the dramaturgical personae and Night magicians gain lore.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is listed among the territories where faux constellations appeared after the Spring Equinox.
t.The Barrens: The Navarri song dreams spread first to the Last Battle Wayhouse in the Barrens, where people of Dawn and some orcs also heard them.
t.Therunin: Overrun by Druj and the vallorn, Therunin has lost the Glimmerwater steading, which fled west with its merrow lantern. Therunin was also untouched by the penumbral veils.
t.Weirwater: Strangers asking for tales of dread were reported on Weirwater's roads, paying ingots for the stories.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: Coral husks are massing here. Bill of Middleton, Keeper of the Dour Fens, must lead a group to cut them down, with lethal force fully justified.
r.Feroz/Morajasse: The Thunderous Deluge reached as far west as Morajasse, drenching the region.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: The flooded Scorrero added to the hardship of reclaiming Oranseri and will make bridging the river harder.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: Coral husks that killed warriors on the coast are hunting the marsh for more dead. The Watcher of Britta's Pool, Rafe, is to stop them.
r.Madruga/Crucible: Night heralds were most often met around Crucible. Its rainbow fountain flooded into a pool that intensifies naga and briar trappings.
r.Madruga/Torres: The cursed rains fell as far north as Torres.
r.Redoubt/Willstone: The Shield of Thought coven of Willstone Citadel submitted Bells of Silver and Brass to the Canterspire Library.
r.Sarvos/Riposi: Riposi's southern cliffs collapsed into the sea during the storms, stripping topsoil from its farms. The region has permanently become coastal.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: Coral husks were sighted near Stark by Jimothy o' Hay. Chancellor Hildebrand Von Holberg is to send Academy cadets to investigate.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Those in Apulus were likely to get lost in unfamiliar parts of the city and stumble into dramatic productions.
r.Therunin/Eastring: The Glimmerwater steading abandoned its flooded Day regio in Eastring after attacks by chikad and vallornspawn husks.

To fight aloud.d: Over half an army's worth of Urizeni military captains swept the mountains with the help of local spires and citadels. Most Disciples made a final stand and were overwhelmed, and several hallowed items were recovered. Severus was captured and brought to Anvil for trial, having agreed to face an inquisition only from the raising priest. Some fugitives were turned away by the Silver Flame or handed over by Tsark, while a few escaped. The Assembly's recognition of the reforged Damakhan's Wisdom drew interest from Leviathan and the Thrice-Cursed Court. Three Sentinel Gate conjunctions were also identified, each offering a chance to intercept fleeing Disciples.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is named as perhaps the only nation where Heralds of the Eternals are seen more often than in Urizen.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are recalled as having once tried to destroy the sword scholars at the Fall of the Four Winds, and the fleeing Ten Echoes coven may be heading for Druj-held Sarangrave.
n.Grendel: The Temple of the Stinging Blade fled south to seek Grendel protection, hoping to trade a powerful blade-oil schema for safe passage. Another group tried to slip into Grendel-held Mareave.
n.The League: Refugees from the Temple of the Inviolate Spirit were turned away by the Silver Flame in League-claimed Spiral and captured. A dozen Wayfarer's Answer Disciples are believed to be hiding somewhere in Spiral.
n.Urizen: Urizen's captains, sentinels and citadels destroyed the Disciples of Sulemaine as an organised group and captured Severus for trial at Anvil. The reforged Damakhan's Wisdom now raises the question of how the nation will preserve Damakhan's legacy.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Kindra Surefoot of Wintermark is among those thanked for helping reforge Damakhan's Wisdom.

t.Mareave: A group of Disciples was trying to cross from Spiral into the rocky hills of Mareave, and an opportunity arose for the Grandmaster of the Sevenfold Path to intercept them there via the Sentinel Gate.
t.Morrow: Captains swept Morrow for Disciple temples. A band carrying a rare dose of true liao was reported heading for Highwatch, possibly intending to create a permanent aura of Purity, and the Polemarch of Highwatch was asked to stop them.
t.Redoubt: The purge began in Redoubt. The Temple of the Stinging Blade fled south from there towards the Grendel, offering the Champion of Loyalty a chance to intercept them.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the Ten Echoes coven from Lustri fled north, apparently heading for the Sarangrave or beyond.
t.Spiral: The Silver Flame in Spiral turned away fleeing Disciples, who were then captured. A dozen Wayfarer's Answer members may be hiding in Spiral, and another group tried to cross from Spiral into Mareave.
t.Zenith: Zenith was the last territory swept by the Urizeni captains, who visited known temples and followed leads from local spires to destroy the Disciples there.

r.Redoubt/Limus: Limus was home to the Temple of the Stinging Blade, famed for its blade oils, whose members fled towards the Grendel with a schema to barter for safe passage.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Refugees from the Temple of the Inviolate Spirit sought shelter with the Silver Flame in Cinion, but were turned away and promptly captured.
r.Zenith/Lustri: Mentioned in passing: the Ten Echoes, a small coven from Lustri, escaped northwards, possibly towards the Sarangrave.

We are the storm.d: Vesna declared the Empire the largest it had ever been after the Sarangrave victory. She called herself 'Ossium's Architect', having developed virgin Druj territory as a senator, and urged citizens to build Imperial homes across former Druj land for new taxes, bourse seats and hearths. She turned to the West, insisting Bregasland is Marcher because the Marchers made their homes there, while the Jotun fight for an ancient idea of the land. She announced she would march with her Iron Sparrows under The Drakes alongside Amberlain P Black and Bregasland's wardens, and invited others to join her. She also named and commended the generals who fought in the Sarangrave.

n.Druj: The Druj were cast as the defeated enemy in the East: Vesna hailed the taking of the Sarangrave as the first blow in a generation-defining war and urged that all former Druj land be settled with Imperial homes.
n.Jotun: Vesna denounced the Jotun presence in Bregasland, saying they fight to relive an ancient victory and are doomed to fail. She vowed that the Empire's enemies would burn if the Jotun did not leave.
n.Varushka: The Empress spoke as a Varushkan, invoking 'my own Varushka' and its tales of Bregasland. She commended generals of Varushkan armies such as the Golden Axe, Northern Eagle and Boyars Hasta for the Sarangrave victory.

t.Bregasland: Vesna claimed Jotun-held Bregasland as Marcher land. She announced that she and her Iron Sparrows would fight there under The Drakes beside Amberlain P Black and Bregasland's wardens, and called on others to join them.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Vesna cited her title 'Ossium's Architect' and her development of Ossium from virgin Druj land as proof that former Druj territory can be built into thriving Imperial land.
t.Sarangrave: The address celebrated the Empire's victory in the Sarangrave as historic, commended the generals who fought there, and pictured Urizeni hearths lighting the territory 'like a constellation of stars'.

What regulates the wheel?.d: Two weeks before the Solstice, a conjunction of the Door, Lock and Key severed the Hall of Worlds from the Imperial regio. A Freeborn magician found the new portal nearby, and the civil service marked it with obsidian stones. Three days before the summit, a Dawnish coven found the regio no longer gave an extra rank of lore. It still speeds rituals, stays a strong regio linked to every territory, and works with the Citadel Guard. A powerful shroud now hides the regio, and the Grandmasters of the Unfettered Mind and Shuttered Lantern were asked to lead the investigation. Every Penumbral Veil and Vale of Shadows across the Empire collapsed, Leviathan moved his visits to midday, and Sung's rituals continued as normal.

n.Dawn: A Dawnish coven that arrived early at Anvil was the first to find the regio's empowering power gone while trying to enchant knights. Dawnish Semmerholm is where the Citadel Guard is stationed.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: news of the broken regio spread to people travelling through Casinea, the territory Highguard holds, and divinations on Casinea were floated as a possible source of clues.
n.Jotun: Every Jotun territory the Empire has maps of, Skallahn, Tromsa and Hordalant, now lies under the strange magnitude 30 shroud. So do the Jotun-held Bregasland and Liathaven.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Therunin, held by Navarr, is named among the territories now covered by the new magnitude 30 shroud.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the shrouds tied to the eternal Sung in Spiral, held by the League, were not affected by the collapse of other concealing magic.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: almost all of Otkodov, held by Thule, is reported to lie under the new magnitude 30 shroud.
n.Urizen: An Urizen seer, Aquillia, foresaw the crisis, and Urizen stargazers revealed the collapse of shrouds and the new shrouds over the Empire. Urizen magicians confirmed the regio still channels rituals through the Citadel Guard, with an unusually strong sense of connection to the army.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland, held by the Jotun, is named among the territories bordering the Empire now covered by a magnitude 30 shroud of unknown origin.
t.Casinea: News of the regio's failure spread like wildfire to those travelling through Casinea to the summit. Some magicians suggested that rituals such as Dreams in the Witch House or Eye of the High Places performed on Casinea might give hints about what happened.
t.Hordalant: Hordalant, a Jotun territory the Empire has mapped, is now covered by the mysterious magnitude 30 shroud.
t.Liathaven: Liathaven, held by the Jotun, is named among the neighbouring territories now covered by the new magnitude 30 shroud.
t.Otkodov: Almost all of Thule-held Otkodov is reported to lie under the new magnitude 30 shroud.
t.Semmerholm: The Citadel Guard is stationed in Semmerholm. Magicians channelling rituals through the army may experience sensory phantoms of the territory, such as Dawnish wine, winter blossoms or glimpses of castles and woods.
t.Skallahn: Skallahn, a mapped Jotun territory, is now covered by the mysterious magnitude 30 shroud.
t.Spiral: The shrouds in Spiral connected to the eternal Sung survived intact while other large-scale concealing magic across the Empire was wiped away.
t.Therunin: Therunin is named among the territories now covered by the new magnitude 30 shroud that seems to blanket the Empire and its surroundings.
t.Tromsa: Tromsa, a mapped Jotun territory, now lies under the mysterious magnitude 30 shroud.

When peace was far away.d: Lord-Magister Anton Trescher wrote candidly that relations could thaw if the Empire respected Jarmish sovereignty, stayed out of the Lantir War and helped against the scions of Cold Sun. Imperial captains now trade at Radosmo in Zemelslo, which the Senate judged a sovereign nation under the Imperial Consul's remit. Zemelslo offered to buy 200 wains of weirwood at 20 crowns each for a navy. Jarm proposed that the Senate expand and concede its embassy in Cargo, garrisoning it with warwizards. The House of the White Palm asked the Apothecaries Guild for 200 drams each of marrowort and bladeroot in return for a herbal. Jarm refused further talk of the shield Measure.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn are cited as distant cousins of the people of Sarvos and the Brass Coast, and a Commonwealth castle in Highguard's Necropolis prompted Jarm's embassy proposal.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the people of Sarvos are cited as cousins to the Highborn, by way of comparison with Zemelslo's kinship to Jarm.
n.Urizen: Jarm proposed that the Senate expand and concede its embassy in Cargo and station elite warwizards there. The Civil Service warned that this would remove Imperial oversight and could leave a hostile Jarmish force inside Urizen if relations collapsed. The Urizeni ritual Ethereal Courier was also named as a way to send weirwood Bourse notes to Zemelslo's intermediary.

t.Necropolis: Jarm cited the Commonwealth castle built in Necropolis, across the river Couros from Cargo, as the reason it wanted a fortified embassy to protect Jarmish emissaries on the river.
t.Redoubt: Jarm proposed that its embassy in Cargo be expanded and conceded, with Jarmish battle-magicians helping to garrison the Walls of Cargo and guard shipping on the Couros against Commonwealth interests.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: its people are given as an example of folk who are cousins to the Highborn, likening this to Zemelslo's ties with Jarm.

r.Redoubt/Limus: The proposed Fortified Embassy commission in Limus would cost 30 mithril and 90 crowns and give the Walls of Cargo the Jarmish Warwizards quality, adding 1,000 strength to the defence if enemies threatened the region. It would require conceding the embassy to Jarm.
